items.title: Sanwo-Olu appoints Akinyemi as acting MD LAWMA
items.description: .Reviews management structure By Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu has finally appointed Olajuwon Akinyemi as the acting Managing Director of the Lagos State Waste Management Authority, LAWMA. By the appointment, Akinyemi succeeded former M.D, Dr. Muyiwa Gbadegesin who was forced to resign following intractable waste management challenges across the state. When contacted, the state Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, on Tuesday evening, confirmed the appointment. According to Wahab, the new MD, who was the former Executive Director of Operations, will also serve in the capacity of Executive Director, Finance. Also, in the coming days, new officers would be redeployed in the restructuring effort of the management staff. This comes following reports of forced resignation of former M.D, Dr. Muyiwa Gbadegesin over the seemingly intractable waste management challenges across the state. This laid to rest earlier reported appointment of , Dr. Hassan Sanuth, Director Sanitation Services – Office of Environment in the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources as acting MD. However, Sanuth was temporarily drafted to LAWMA to assist in waste management pending appointment of substantive managing director. On October 19, indications emerged that Governor Sanwo-Olu has directed Gbadegesin to resign amid persistent refuse accumulation across the state. It was gathered that the governor became increasingly dissatisfied with Gbadegesin’s handling of the waste management crisis and had asked him to step down. Earlier in September 2026, during an inspection of the Olusosun Dumpsite in Ojota, Sanwo-Olu handed a strong warning against further failure to stop the menace announcing plans to overhaul the agency for effective management, describing Gbadegesin’s inability as “sabotage” According to an inside source, “the governor’s displeasure stemmed from the slow pace of waste evacuation and the alleged failure of Gbadegesin to act promptly on directives aimed at addressing the crisis. “The governor was at the Olusosun Dumpsite in Ojota a month ago and was dissatisfied with the state of things. He gave instructions that immediate action be taken on the matter, as he has declared a state of emergency on waste management. “The governor was upset when he observed that the situation had not improved despite his clear directive. So, over the weekend, he asked him to resign, although he is begging and has reached out to some prominent Lagosians to beg on his behalf.” Also, residents across Lagos have repeatedly complained about worsening waste collection, with refuse accumulating along road medians, streets and major highways. The prevalent parts of the state, include: Ogba, Idimu, Ejigbo, Mushin, Egbeda, Surulere, Ajegunle, Ikorodu, Ojo, Obalende, Apapa and Mile 2, where residents have had to contend with heaps of stinking refuse along streets and drainage channels. The situation has raised concerns about environmental sanitation, public health, the impact on businesses and the state’s image. Akinyemi, an indigene of Badagry Local Government Area and seasoned administrator was appointed by President Bola Tinubu in 2025 as the Deputy Executive Secretary (Technical) for Universal Basic Education Commission. Before the appointment, he served as Deputy Executive Secretary (Technical) in the Lagos State Civil Service for UBEC. He also served as the state’s Director of Administration and Human Resources in the Office of Infrastructure. The post Sanwo-Olu appoints Akinyemi as acting MD LAWMA appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Embrace HIV testing as routine healthcare-Lagos govt urges residents
items.description: . Extends free screening to staff, trade fair visitors By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has urged residents across the state to embrace HIV testing as part of routine healthcare rather than wait until they suspect an infection before seeking screening. Meanwhile, the state government has extended free HIV testing and counselling services to public servants and visitors to the ongoing 2026 International Trade Fair as part of efforts to promote early diagnosis and expand access to HIV prevention and treatment. The interventions, implemented by the Lagos State AIDS Control Agency (LSACA), are aimed at bringing HIV-related services closer to residents, encouraging routine testing and ensuring that individuals who require further care are linked to appropriate treatment facilities. At the Public Service Week health screening exercise, the Head of Service, Lagos State, Mr Bode Agoro, officially opened the free screening programme and urged public servants to prioritise their health by taking advantage of the opportunity. Agoro said access to preventive healthcare, including HIV screening, was essential to building a healthy, productive and efficient workforce. He encouraged workers to embrace regular health checks and utilise the confidential testing, professional counselling and information on HIV prevention, transmission and treatment provided through the exercise. In a related intervention, LSACA commenced free HIV testing and counselling services at the Lagos Pavilion, Tafawa Balewa Square (TBS), as part of activities at the 2026 International Trade Fair. The exercise, which began on Friday, November 6, is scheduled to run for 10 days, ending on Sunday, November 15. It provides visitors, exhibitors, traders and other participants with access to confidential HIV screening, counselling, preventive health information and guidance on accessing treatment and care where necessary. The Chief Executive Officer of LSACA, Dr Folakemi Animashaun, reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to ensuring that HIV prevention, testing and treatment services remain accessible, confidential and free from discrimination. Animashaun said knowing one’s HIV status was an important step towards preventing new infections and improving health outcomes, noting that early diagnosis enables individuals who test positive to commence treatment promptly and maintain healthy, productive lives. She urged public servants, Trade Fair participants and residents across the state to embrace HIV testing as part of routine healthcare rather than wait until they suspect an infection before seeking screening. The LSACA chief executive also emphasised the importance of collaboration with Ministries, Departments and Agencies, development partners, civil society organisations and other stakeholders in expanding access to HIV prevention, testing, treatment and care services. Animashaun therefore, urged members of the public to visit the LSACA screening centre at the Lagos Pavilion, Tafawa Balewa Square, to access the ongoing free testing and counselling exercise. She added that similar services were available at designated health facilities across the state. items.title: US calls for new Europe security framework as Russia, Ukraine hold first peace talks in 9 months
items.description: A first day of US-led talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi ended on Tuesday, with Washington calling for a “new” security framework, as Europe fears US President Donald Trump plans a deal with Moscow on the continent’s future. Trump’s envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff brought together the warring sides for several hours of negotiations — the first since February — that are set to continue on Wednesday. Kushner told delegates the United States had “narrowed the gaps” between the sides — without providing details — and hoped to move towards a “solution” to Europe’s worst conflict since World War II. In Paris, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio hailed the talks as “very productive” and called for Europeans to be eventually included at the negotiating table “because they are part of solving this problem”. Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy later said the talks were “constructive and quite substantive”, saying his team reported to him that humanitarian issues and security guarantees were among what was discussed. Speaking in Copenhagen, the Ukrainian president also said it was “time” for Europe to choose a representative for the talks. Europe has been rattled as Trump has floated a deal with Russia on rewriting Europe’s post-war security, also worrying that Washington will force Kyiv to accept a de facto defeat. At the Abu Dhabi talks, Trump’s son-in-law Kushner said the US hoped to “create a new framework” of security between Ukraine, Russia and Europe that will secure “decades, if not centuries, of peace”. Moscow , which several weeks before invading Ukraine issued an ultimatum to Western countries to roll back troops from eastern Europe, had also said this was a priority. Ukraine has warned against a “Yalta 2.0”, referring to Western leaders dividing Europe with the Soviet Union after World War II, and the EU has said security arrangements can only be discussed after a ceasefire. “Putin wants the USSR back,” Zelensky told Danish media. Russia, which occupies swathes of its smaller neighbour, pummelled Ukraine with more attacks overnight, cutting power to thousands as temperatures plummet. Putin has repeatedly turned down broader ceasefire offers and vowed his troops will press on in Ukraine. Moscow pushes security review In a sign it is serious about reviving its demand to review Europe’s decades-old security arrangement, Russia included a diplomat — Sergei Ryabkov — who logged Moscow’s pre-invasion demand for Nato to pull back from eastern Europe. A Russian delegation source had said that settling the war was “merely one item on the agenda” and that Moscow’s main objective was reviewing security “for the entire continent”. Kyiv’s chief negotiator Rustem Umerov met the US envoys and European, EU and Nato officials before the negotiations. Nato’s general in Europe, Alexus Grynkewich, is also taking part. In a joint statement, the Europeans, Ukraine, US and Nato reaffirmed their “shared commitment to a strong post-war European security architecture”. Ukraine pushes for truces Umerov said Kyiv’s priorities remained securing a ceasefire and security guarantees. “Our people are waiting to end this war,” he said. As talks continued, Ukrainian and French foreign ministers in Paris commended US efforts to push for “partial truces”, which could serve as a “first step toward a complete and unconditional ceasefire”. Last month, a local truce in Ukraine’s Kherson region brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump became the longest pause in fighting during the war. Kyiv is also pushing post-war support for its army. A senior Ukrainian source told AFP that Ukraine wanted at least 10 years of financial support to sustain an 800,000-strong army able to defend any future Russian attack. Land issue There is huge distrust in Ukraine towards Trump’s aims. The US leader hinted before the talks that Kyiv might have to give up land, saying: “They’re going to end up with a little bit different shape.” Russia’s troops have advanced westward but have not been able to seize the whole of the coveted Donetsk region , and Moscow demands Kyiv surrender the parts of the embattled area it controls. “Allowing Russia to decide the borders of Europe will be a huge mistake,” Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen said, as she hosted Zelensky on Tuesday. The Ukrainian leader is due to meet other Nordic leaders in Denmark and earlier spoke to Finland’s Alexander Stubb, telling him Kyiv’s negotiators are doing their “best” to ensure talks “deliver results”. Stubb is rumoured to be one of the contenders who could represent Europe at negotiations to end the war. The Finnish leader and Norway’s Jonas Gahr Støre held a rare phone call with Putin last month, which they called “frank and substantive”.

items.title: Gov’t considers legal backing for GES Code of Conduct – Education Minister
items.description: The Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, says the government is considering elevating the Ghana Education Service (GES) Code of Conduct into legislation to ensure teachers who engage in misconduct are dealt with decisively and in accordance with the law. The move follows an incident involving two teachers at Pepease D/A Junior High School (JHS) in the Ashanti Region, who reportedly engaged in a physical fight on the school premises. Speaking in Parliament on Tuesday, November 10, Mr Iddrisu said the GES had been directed to investigate the incident and ensure that appropriate disciplinary action was taken against the teachers. “Mr Speaker, on this specific matter, in many instances, government has resolved to elevate the Ghana Education Service Code of Conduct to a level of legislation to ensure that culprits are dealt with decisively and in accordance with the law,” he told Parliament. He stressed that the GES takes incidents of unprofessional conduct among teachers seriously, particularly when they occur in the presence of students. On the Pepease D/A JHS incident, the Minister said the Ashanti Regional Director of Education had been instructed to conduct a formal investigation and submit the findings to the Director-General of the GES. He added that disciplinary proceedings would be initiated in line with the GES Code of Conduct and the Public Services Regulations. “Mr Speaker, we will ensure that the GES investigates the matter and appropriate sanctions are applied,” he assured the House.

items.title: ‎States must contribute to pension protection fund to benefit from minimum pension — PenCom DG
items.description: ‎–It is big shame for some state retirees to be paid ₦5,000’ ‎‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎‎ABUJA — The Director-General of Nigeria’s National Pension Commission (PenCom), Ms. Omolola Bridget Oloworaran, said on Tuesday that states must contribute to the Pension Protection Fund before they can become eligible for the minimum pension. ‎‎She stated this at the official launch of the Minimum Pension Guarantee Scheme and the unveiling of PenCare, a pension industry-funded healthcare initiative designed to provide low-income retirees with access to essential medical services free of charge. ‎‎The event was held at the Old Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja. ‎She said about 170,000 retirees are expected to receive the minimum pension of ₦52,500, including those who were previously receiving less than that amount. ‎‎“Every eligible retiree who earns below ₦52,500 will be uplifted to ₦52,500. So, of course, as I said, there is no discrimination if you are within the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS). ‎‎“However, there is an eligibility criterion at the same level. We are making it a requirement that states must contribute to the Pension Protection Fund before they can be eligible for the minimum pension. ‎‎“So, we will work out that modality at the state level because we all know that the fund needs to be sustainable. If people are not contributing, we will run out of funds, and we cannot start a laudable initiative like this and then, years from now, somebody says it has stopped working because people are not contributing. ‎‎“So, we are working on modalities for the states to start contributing. But, as of now, it does not apply only to federal workers. Even private-sector workers are receiving these minimum pensions. ‎‎“As I said in my speech, 54 per cent of the total number of retirees who fall below the minimum pension work in the private sector, even though the private sector is not the majority employer. Essentially, 65 per cent or more of private-sector retirees are earning less than ₦52,500. ‎‎“So, when we tell them to contribute to the Pension Protection Fund, there is a reason for that. They form a large chunk of the money we need.” ‎‎On whether anything was being done to ensure that retirees from states also benefit from the minimum pension, as some of them still receive about ₦5,000 monthly, the PenCom DG said it was shameful to pay someone such an amount, although she doubted whether any state actually paid such a paltry sum. ‎‎“Frankly, that is a big shame. What we have done is that we have started working with the states to ensure that they pay retirement benefits to their retirees and also put a plan in place to review pensionable inflation. ‎‎“I mean, receiving ₦5,000 is unacceptable. I do hope it is not true. I will ask my team to confirm. ‎‎“But ultimately, what we are trying to do is get all the states into the scheme. Once you get into the scheme and start contributing to the Pension Protection Fund, the fund can protect the retirees of those who participate.” ‎‎She expressed joy that many Nigerians, especially retirees, had started receiving the minimum pension. ‎She also said that the Commission had given healthcare cards to some people to test the system before the official launch. ‎‎“Because, before you pilot something, you want to test it with a group of people to make sure that it is working as intended. So, it has been rolled out, and Nigerians can now go into a hospital and enjoy free healthcare. ‎‎“So, as I said, what we did today was symbolic. But from today, anybody who does not have their card can go to their PFA and request one.” ‎‎Answering a question on why the Commission decided to launch the service when elections were forthcoming, and whether it was not a plot to influence voters, the DG said she did not involve herself in politics. ‎‎She rhetorically asked: “Is there ever a bad time to do good for ordinary Nigerians, to put a smile on people’s faces? And you know, I do not get involved in politics. I never talk about politicians or anything political. We just do our work.” ‎‎She said PenCom was only a regulator. ‎“We do not get involved in politics at all. You can ask my people. But my response to that will be: every day you wake up, we try to see what we can do to improve the lives of ordinary Nigerians. When we did the pension boost last year, there was no election. ‎‎“She also said that the Commission had paid a ₦32,000 consequential increase last year when there was no election. ‎‎“It is not something that is geared towards the election. It just happens to be coming at this point. In fact, this was supposed to be done in September when we were expecting the President himself to attend, but the industry said we needed to do some other things, and we shifted Pension Week to October. ‎‎“You will notice that we had said this was going to be done in October, but we could not do it then. So, we shifted it from September to October because of the industry. Later, we decided to settle for today. ‎‎“So, everything we are doing, we are just doing our work. We do not see elections. I do not. Frankly, anybody else might see it, but I am responsible for PenCom. I do not see elections. I do not see competition. I am just doing my work. ‎‎“But guess what? If my work makes the President look good, then it means I am doing what he hired me to do. And on that question, I will also say this: I have been going for press conferences, and people ask me, ‘You are doing all of this. How are you going to make sure it is sustainable?’ Even then, when I am supposed to talk politics, I still do not talk politics. You understand? So, we do not do politics here. ‎‎“But, to be fair, it is a President who has appointed the right person to lead, who has appointed the right board and leadership in PenCom, and we are executing his vision for the industry. That is how I see it. And lastly, I would just say: does it matter what time it is, provided ordinary Nigerians are benefiting?” The post ‎States must contribute to pension protection fund to benefit from minimum pension — PenCom DG appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: KNUST Researcher investigates how AI can improve brain scan analysis
items.description: How well can artificial intelligence developed using medical data from Europe and North America analyse brain scans from Ghanaian patients? This question took Ghanaian biomedical engineer Dr Prince Ebenezer Adjei to the German Cancer Research Centre (DKFZ) in Heidelberg, where he worked with researchers to investigate how medical imaging AI tools perform on Ghanaian clinical scans. Dr Adjei, who leads the Global Health AI Lab ( GHAiC-K ) at the Global Health and Infectious Diseases Group of the Kumasi Centre for Collaborative Research in Tropical Medicine ( GHID-KCCR ), has returned from the research visit with early findings that could inform the development of medical AI tools for Ghanaian healthcare. Dr. Prince Ebenezer Adjei Working with colleagues at DKFZ, he used approximately 1,600 unlabelled head CT scans from Ghana for further training of AI models through a method known as self-supervised learning. This allows models to learn patterns from medical images without requiring specialists to manually label every scan. The work involved nnFoundation, one of DKFZ’s newer medical imaging AI tools, and nnU-Net, an established framework developed at the same institution. The researchers tested the approaches on tasks including identifying areas of brain damage caused by acute stroke and estimating a person’s brain age. The preliminary results suggest that the benefits of additional AI training depend on the task being performed. For identifying stroke damage and estimating brain age, nnFoundation did not outperform the nnU-Net approach trained on Ghanaian scans, although it showed an advantage in some other tasks. Dr Adjei, who is also a lecturer with the Biomedical Engineering programme at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi (KNUST) and a fellow of the Responsible Artificial Intelligence Lab (RAIL), noted that one of the clearest lessons concerned the quality of the data. “What surprised me was how much the quality of our data mattered. Clear, accurate examples improved results more than anything else. Large strokes were easy for the AI to find; small ones were much harder,” he said. The work has also left him with a question he intends to pursue: “Can we build good AI for Ghana without needing thousands of scans labelled by busy specialists?” Preparing medical scans for AI research often requires specialists to identify abnormalities or outline affected areas. This can take considerable time, making it difficult to assemble the large datasets needed for developing and testing medical imaging tools. The researchers are now investigating how much labelled data is necessary. Through a series of experiments described as a “label ladder”, they are testing how the models perform when trained with different quantities of annotated scans. The aim is to establish whether additional training using unlabelled Ghanaian scans can reduce the amount of specialist labelling required. Could AI help doctors detect strokes faster? A brain scan is an important part of diagnosing stroke. It helps doctors determine whether a patient has a blocked or bleeding blood vessel, information needed when deciding on treatment. Dr Adjei believes AI could eventually help doctors interpret these scans more quickly, particularly in hospitals where radiologists are not readily available. “One day, when a patient arrives with a suspected stroke, AI could check their brain scan within minutes and alert doctors to the problem. This could speed up treatment, especially in hospitals with few or no radiologists,” he said. However, the tools would need further testing before they could be introduced into routine clinical care. Dr Adjei also wants greater attention paid to how AI is regulated in healthcare, particularly regarding patient information, the training of health professionals and the responsibility of doctors using such systems. “Before that happens, Ghana’s existing data protection laws need to be updated for AI, and the national AI health policy must be put into practice. Health workers will need training, the tools must be tested in many Ghanaian hospitals, with doctors always making the final decision.” Maintaining research partnership Dr Adjei undertook the research visit through the inaugural Global Research Opportunities for the South (GROW) programme of the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD). The programme, funded by Germany’s Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, supports researchers from developing countries to undertake research in Germany and establish international scientific partnerships. At DKFZ, he worked under the supervision of Dr Fabian Isensee, a medical image computing researcher and one of the developers of nnU-Net, a framework widely used in medical image analysis. Although Dr Adjei has returned to Ghana, the research is continuing. “Our findings are still early and not yet conclusive, so the work continues. We are still working with the team in DKFZ on the questions this visit raised,” he said. The researchers are conducting larger, repeated experiments using DKFZ’s computing cluster. They also plan to examine additional tasks, including detecting bleeding in the brain and retrieving relevant medical images from datasets. In Ghana, Dr Adjei’s team is working with Spectra Health Imaging Limited to build a larger collection of high-quality Ghanaian brain scans for further research. The work forms part of the activities of the Global Health AI Lab at GHID-KCCR, which Dr Adjei leads, and provides opportunities for young researchers to gain experience in medical imaging and AI. “For KNUST, GHAICK (GHID-KCCR) and young Ghanaian researchers, this partnership opens doors to world-class expertise and tools and helps build AI made with African data for African patients,” he said. The next stage of the research will establish whether the early findings hold across larger experiments and whether additional training on Ghanaian scans can reduce the need for extensive manual annotation.

items.title: Élim CAN 2027 : les Lions de l’Atlas poursuivent leur préparation avant le double duel face au Niger
items.description: Les Lions de l’Atlas ont effectué mardi leur deuxième séance d’entraînement au Complexe Mohammed VI de Football à Maâmora, à trois jours de leur premier rendez-vous face au Niger dans le cadre des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. La sélection nationale poursuit sa préparation sous la conduite de Mohamed Ouahbi en vue de la double confrontation face au Niger, prévue les 13 et 17 novembre prochains. La séance de ce mardi, organisée de 17h00 à 18h30, s’est déroulée en présence de l’ensemble des joueurs convoqués. Le staff technique a consacré le travail aux volets physique, technique et tactique, avec notamment des exercices de circulation du ballon, des séquences de jeu collectif et des mises en place tactiques. Dans une ambiance studieuse, les joueurs ont affiché concentration et engagement à l’approche de ces deux rencontres importantes pour la suite des qualifications. Après les deux premières journées, le Maroc occupe la première place du groupe A avec six points. Le Gabon et le Niger suivent avec trois points chacun, tandis que le Lesotho ferme la marche avec zéro point. Les Lions de l’Atlas auront donc l’occasion de conforter leur position de leader lors de cette double confrontation face au Niger. Le premier match aura lieu vendredi 13 novembre à 20h00 GMT au Complexe Sportif Mohammed V de Casablanca. Les deux équipes se retrouveront quatre jours plus tard, mardi 17 novembre, au Complexe Sportif Prince Moulay Abdellah de Rabat, avec un coup d’envoi également fixé à 20h00 GMT. Ces deux rendez-vous constituent les prochaines échéances de la sélection marocaine dans sa course à la qualification pour la Coupe d’Afrique des Nations 2027. The post Élim CAN 2027 : les Lions de l’Atlas poursuivent leur préparation avant le double duel face au Niger appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: GIPA CEO calls for shift from raw material exports to value addition
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA), Simon Madjie, has called for a shift from raw material exports towards value addition to accelerate Ghana’s industrial transformation. According to him, Ghana must leverage its mineral and cocoa resources to develop local industries, create jobs and strengthen control over its natural resources. Mr Madjie made the call at the 15th Ghana Economic Forum, hosted by the Business and Financial Times (B&FT) in Accra, under the theme “From Stabilisation to Scale: Mobilising Capital, Technology and Policy for Ghana’s Next Industrial Wave.” He said moving beyond raw material exports by 2030 required deliberate efforts to attract investment and expand domestic processing capacity. According to him, natural resources should serve as a foundation for industrial development rather than being treated solely as commodities for export. Mr Madjie emphasised the importance of attracting international private capital, noting that investors were expected to pay taxes, create jobs, transfer technology and operate responsibly in exchange for access to Ghana’s markets and natural resources. He urged foreign investors to integrate Ghanaian businesses into their value chains to build local capacity and competitiveness. The GIPA CEO also highlighted the need for legal and regulatory reforms to strengthen investor protection and reduce barriers to doing business. However, he stressed that reforms must be supported by an enabling business environment that encouraged collaboration between local and foreign investors. He said stronger partnerships, technology transfer and local participation were essential to building Ghanaian businesses and sustaining long-term industrial growth.

items.title: JOJ Dakar | Taekwondo : Médaille d’argent historique pour Yasmine Haouani
items.description: La jeune taekwondoïste Yasmine Haouani a décroché une médaille d'argent historique aux Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse (JOJ) de Dakar 2026, ce mardi 10 novembre. C'est ce qu'annonce le ministère de la Jeunesse et des Sports, en félicitant la jeune médaillée engagée dans la catégorie des -55 kg lors de la 11e journée des compétitions. Après de belles victoire, la championne tunisienne s'est inclinée en finale face à la Sénégalaise Marie Sarr sur le score de deux rounds à zéro (4-8, 3-11). « Cette remarquable performance constitue la deuxième médaille de l'histoire du taekwondo tunisien aux JOJ, après la médaille de bronze remportée par le champion olympique Mohamed Khalil Jendoubi lors de l'édition de Buenos Aires en 201 8 », se réjouit le ministère des Sports. La même source rappelle par ailleurs qu'il s'agit de la deuxième médaille d'argent décrochée par la Tunisie au cours de ces Jeux Olympiques de Dakar, après le succès de l'athlète Katr El Nada Gouad dans l'épreuve du lancer du disque. items.title: Rabat: Hammouchi inaugure un centre intégré de médecine dentaire
items.description: Le Directeur général du pôle DGST-DGSN, Abdellatif Hammouchi, a inauguré, mardi à Rabat, un nouveau centre médical intégré spécialisé en médecine dentaire, destiné à fournir des soins de qualité au profit des fonctionnaires de la Sûreté nationale et de la Surveillance du territoire, ainsi qu'aux retraités et ayants droit, et ce dans le cadre de l'attention sociale et de la prise en charge sanitaire constante portée aux ressources humaines policières. La création de ce centre sanitaire de qualité s'inscrit dans le prolongement du Centre de radiologie et d'analyses médicales de la Sûreté nationale, inauguré par le Roi Mohammed VI en 2019, indique un communiqué du pôle DGSN-DGST. Les services dispensés par ce Centre se sont considérablement élargis pour intégrer des examens et des consultations médicales avancées, dans le cadre d'un processus de développement continu qui incarne une vision stratégique ambitieuse visant à instaurer un système de santé moderne, performant et accessible à l'ensemble de la famille de la Sûreté nationale. Le nouveau centre de médecine dentaire a été équipé selon les normes et standards internationaux les plus élevés en matière de médecine et de chirurgie dentaires, à travers des équipements techniques de pointe reposant sur la numérisation et l'intelligence artificielle médicale, afin de fournir un environnement thérapeutique intégré combinant précision, célérité et sécurité des patients. Ce centre comprend neuf salles de soins dotées de fauteuils médicaux dentaires modernes, de systèmes de radiographie numérique intra-orale (RVG) et de scanners intra-oraux 3D, outre une salle dédiée à la radiologie équipée d'un appareil panoramique, et une unité de stérilisation soumise aux règles d'hygiène et de lutte contre les infections les plus strictes, ainsi qu'un laboratoire intégré de prothèses dentaires appuyé par des systèmes de conception et de fabrication assistées par ordinateur (CAD/CAM) et des imprimantes 3D. Le nouveau centre offre une large gamme de traitements et d'interventions spécialisés, incluant l’odontologie conservatrice, la chirurgie buccale, ainsi que les prothèses dentaires fixes et amovibles en céramique et en zircone, en plus de fournir des services d'orthodontie pour les enfants de moins de seize ans, sous la supervision d'un staff médical et paramédical spécialisé qui veille au confort des patients. Ce nouveau centre marque un jalon fondamental dans le cadre d’une feuille de route ambitieuse pour développer et rapprocher l’offre de santé des fonctionnaires de la police au niveau régional. Dans ce sens, des centres de santé similaires verront le jour prochainement à Tanger et à Marrakech, l’étape technique ayant été achevée, tandis que les travaux de réalisation ont débuté, l’objectif étant d’élargir la base des bénéficiaires et de faciliter leur accès aux consultations de base et celles de pointe, ainsi qu’aux soins spécialisés dans les différentes régions du Royaume. Ce projet vital s'inscrit dans la stratégie globale adoptée par le Pôle DGSN-DGST visant à instaurer un système de santé et social intégré plaçant l’élément humain au cœur de ses priorités. Cette vision, conclut le communiqué, consiste à offrir une gamme complète de consultations médicales, d’examens en laboratoire et de traitements spécialisés de qualité au profit des membres de la famille de la sûreté nationale, aussi bien ceux en service que les retraités, partant de la conviction que la mise à disposition d’une protection sanitaire avancée et durable constitue un pilier essentiel pour réaliser la stabilité sociale et psychologique des fonctionnaires de la sûreté nationale, et un catalyseur pour renforcer leur rendement professionnel au service de la sécurité de la patrie et des citoyens. The post Rabat: Hammouchi inaugure un centre intégré de médecine dentaire appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ashanti GES investigates two Pepease D/A JHS teachers over fight – Haruna Iddrisu
items.description: The Ashanti Regional Directorate of Education has opened an investigation into the conduct of two teachers at Pepease D/A Junior High School (JHS) following an incident in which they allegedly fought on the school premises. The Education Minister, Haruna Iddrisu, disclosed this in Parliament on Tuesday, November 10, saying the Regional Director of Education had been directed to conduct a formal investigation and submit the findings to the Director-General of the Ghana Education Service (GES). “Regarding the incident at Pepease D/A JHS, the Ashanti Regional Director of Education has been directed to conduct a formal investigation into the incident and submit the findings to the Director-General of GES,” he said. He added that disciplinary proceedings would be initiated against the teachers in accordance with the GES Code of Conduct and the Public Services Regulation. “The Ghana Education Service takes all incidents of unprofessional conduct among teachers very seriously, particularly where said conduct occurs in the presence of students,” Mr Iddrisu said. The Minister further assured Parliament that the GES would investigate the matter and ensure that appropriate sanctions were applied. “Mr Speaker, we will ensure that the GES investigates the matter and appropriate sanctions are applied,” he stated. Mr Iddrisu also disclosed that the government was considering giving the GES Code of Conduct legislative backing to strengthen the Service’s ability to deal with misconduct among teachers. “Mr Speaker, on this specific matter, in many instances, government has resolved to elevate the Ghana Education Service Code of Conduct to a level of legislation to ensure that culprits are dealt with decisively and in accordance with law,” he said.

items.title: FIFA : Arsène Wenger envisage de défier Gianni Infantino pour la présidence
items.description: La succession de Gianni Infantino à la tête de la Fédération internationale de football association (FIFA) pourrait prendre une nouvelle tournure. Le Français Arsène Wenger réfléchit sérieusement à la possibilité de briguer la présidence de l'instance mondiale et de se mesurer au dirigeant suisse lors de l'élection prévue en mars 2027. L'information a été révélée ce mardi 10 novembre par la BBC. Selon le média britannique, l'ancien manager d'Arsenal, âgé de 77 ans, est depuis plusieurs semaines sollicité par des responsables du football européen qui souhaitent lui voir porter une candidature face à Infantino. Son éventuelle entrée dans la course pourrait bénéficier du soutien de l'Union européenne des associations de football (UEFA), particulièrement critique à l'égard de l'actuel président de la FIFA. Toutefois, aucune décision définitive n'a encore été prise par le technicien français. La candidature de Wenger intervient dans un contexte de tensions autour de la gouvernance de la FIFA. Gianni Infantino a notamment essuyé de vives critiques après son projet, finalement abandonné, de céder une participation commerciale dans une structure liée à la Coupe du monde à des investisseurs privés. Une initiative qui avait provoqué des désaccords avec plusieurs confédérations, notamment l'UEFA. Wenger avait lui-même pris ses distances avec ce projet, affirmant ne pas avoir été associé à son élaboration et défendant une FIFA indépendante et transparente. Mais le Suisse conserve des soutiens importants. Il a notamment obtenu l'appui des 54 associations nationales africaines, ainsi que des soutiens en Asie et en Amérique du Sud. Sa réélection pour un quatrième mandat reste donc une perspective sérieuse. Pour Wenger, dont la crédibilité et l'expérience du football international constituent des atouts, le défi sera de parvenir à fédérer suffisamment de voix. Il devra également clarifier ses intentions avant le 18 novembre 2026, date limite de déclaration des candidatures. L'ancien sélectionneur du Japon, Kozo Tashima, et l'ancien défenseur de Tottenham, Ramon Vega, ont également manifesté leur intention de briguer le poste. Le scrutin est prévu le 18 mars 2027 à Rabat, au Maroc, lors du Congrès de la FIFA. Une échéance qui pourrait donner lieu à une bataille électorale particulièrement disputée.

items.title: Awujale stool: Adele-in-Council sues Abiodun, challenges reconstituted interregnum committee
items.description: By James Ogunnaike Abeokuta The Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council has dragged the Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, and members of the reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council before the state High Court, Ijebu-Ode, challenging what it described as an unlawful attempt to displace the traditional administrative structure of Ijebuland. Other defendants sued alongside Gov Abiodun are the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs as well as members of the recently reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council including High Chief Rasheed Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu Ode, Chief Chris Okunowo, the Bobasuwa, Prof Jide Ajayi, the Jagun Aso, Chief Stephen Bakare, the Babalaje as well as Chief Alade Shote, the Otun Balogun The suit dated November 5, 2026 and marked HCJ/201/2026 according to a statement from the Media office of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council and supporting court documents made available to journalists on Tuesday seeks to establish the authority of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council to oversee the traditional and administrative affairs of Ijebu-Ode during the interregnum following the transition of the late Awujale of Ijebuland, Oba Sikiru Kayode Adetona. The nine members of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council led by the Adele and Ogbeni Oja of Ijebuland, Olorogun Dr Sonny Kuku, are asking the court to declare that the Adele system is the only legitimate traditional administrative authority recognised by the native law, customs and ancestral practices of the Ijebu people during the period between the reigns of successive Awujales. They are also challenging the establishment and subsequent reconstitution of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council, describing the arrangement as alien to Ijebu customary law and inconsistent with the Ogun State Chiefs Law. In the substantive suit, the plaintiffs are seeking a declaration that neither the state governor nor the relevant government authorities possess the power to create or reconstitute an administrative council capable of displacing the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council during an interregnum. They are further asking the court to set aside the purported reconstitution of the AIAC and the appointments of the fifth to eighth defendants, describing the appointments as irregular, illegal, unconstitutional, null and void. The plaintiffs also want a perpetual injunction restraining the governor, the relevant ministries and other government officials from interfering with or bypassing the customary administrative functions of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council. Similarly, they are seeking an order restraining the reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council from holding meetings, parading themselves or exercising traditional, civil or financial administrative authority over Ijebu-Ode under the disputed AIAC arrangement. The statement partly reads the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council is hereby seeking “A declaration that under the native law, custom, tradition, and ancestral usages of the Ijebu-Ode people, the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council is the sole, valid, and historically recognized traditional administrative authority entitled to manage the interim traditional and local administrative affairs of Ijebu-Ode during an interregnum following the transition of the Awujale of Ijebuland. “A declaration that the unilateral creation, establishment, or reconstitution of an administrative body known as the “Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council” (AIAC) by the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Defendants is alien, unknown, and offensive to the native law, customs, traditions, and ancestral usages of the Ijebu-Ode people, and completely inconsistent with the provisions of the Chiefs Law of Ogun State. “A declaration that neither the Chiefs Law of Ogun State nor any applicable customary law empowers the 1st to 3rd Defendants to arbitrarily invent, sustain, or reconstitute an “Interregnum Administrative Council” to sideline, supplant, or replace the ancestral Adele system and traditional council structures during an interregnum” The plaintiffs are also asking for “an order setting aside the purported reconstitution of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC) and the handpicked appointments of the 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, and 8th Defendants by the 1st to 3rd Defendants as highly irregular, illegal, unconstitutional, null, void, and of no effect whatsoever. “An order of permanent injunction restraining the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Defendants, whether by themselves, their agents, officials, ministries, or privies, from interfering with, bypassing, or disrupting the customary administrative functions of the Plaintiffs as the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council during the period of the interregnum. “An order of permanent injunction restraining the 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, and 8th Defendants from holding meetings, parading themselves, or attempting to exercise any traditional, civil, or financial administration over the town and stool of Ijebu-Ode under the guise or authority of the illegal, purported newly reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC)” It would be recalled that traditional chiefs in Ijebu-Ode and members of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council, constituted by the state government in August last year following the death of the Awujale and paramount ruler of Ijebuland, Oba Sikiru Adetona, recently resolved to dissolve the council and transition into the Adele Oba Awujale in Council to oversee the affairs of the ancient town pending the emergence of a substantive Awujale. The decision was reportedly reached at a meeting involving the Ilamuren, Pampa, Odi and other chiefs of Ijebu-Ode, where the traditional leaders unanimously adopted a resolution mandating members of the AIAC to step down from their existing positions and assume membership of the newly constituted Adele Oba Awujale in Council. According to the resolution signed by the Chairman of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council, Olo’rgun Dr Sonny Kuku, the chiefs said the decision to transition from the interregnum administration to the Adele Oba Awujale in Council was informed by their consideration of the existing traditional and statutory frameworks governing the Awujale chieftaincy institution. The government had however announced the reconstitution of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC), reaffirming its legal authority to oversee the administrative and traditional affairs of Ijebuland pending the appointment and coronation of a new Awujale Addressing the emergence of the Adele Oba Awujale group, the government declared that “the body had no legal or customary recognition under the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration or the existing chieftaincy legislation in Ogun State”. It stated further that “neither the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration nor the Obas and Chiefs Law of Ogun State 2021 makes provision for an Adele Oba Awujale group or assigns it any recognised responsibility in the management of the Awujale stool”. The government thereafter announced the reconstitution of the council with the following members; Chief Rasheed Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode – Chairman, Chief Chris Okunowo, the Bobasuwa as Secretary, while Prof. Jide Ajayi, Jagun Aso, Chief Stephen O. Bakare, Babalaje and Chief Alade Shote, Otun Balogun are to serve as members. The government said the reconstituted council would continue to discharge the legally recognised administrative and traditional responsibilities of the AIAC until a new Awujale was appointed and crowned. The Fusengbuwa ruling house had earlier dragged Abiodun, the Awujale kingmakers and five others before the High Court sitting in Ijebu-Ode, seeking orders compelling the completion of the process for the selection of the next Awujale and Paramount Ruler of Ijebuland. The Awujale stool became vacant in July 2025 following the death of Oba Sikiru Adetona at the age of 91, after 65 years on the throne. The Ogun State government halted the selection process in January 2026, citing petitions from security agencies and stakeholders, following an earlier suspension over procedural concerns in December 2025. A total of 95 aspirants—94 princes and one princess—emerged from the ruling house nomination process held in Ijebu-Ode in December before the government halted the selection process The post Awujale stool: Adele-in-Council sues Abiodun, challenges reconstituted interregnum committee appeared first on Vanguard News .

Only Rainbow Coalition can guarantee Tinubu’s victory in Bayelsa – PDP
items.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa The Peoples Democratic Party ,PDP, in Bayelsa State has claimed that the Rainbow Coalition is central to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election prospects in the state, pledging to mobilise 300,000 votes for the President in the 2027 general elections. The state PDP chairman and leader of the coalition, Chief George Alabh Turnah, made the declaration in a statement issued by his Senior Special Assistant on Media and Communication, Kevin Loveday-Egbo. Turnah said the coalition would take its campaign for Tinubu’s re-election to communities across the state, with a grassroots mobilisation strategy targeting undecided voters ahead of the 2027 elections. He described the National Rainbow Coalition as a platform for engaging voters, explaining that the group would use its community-level outreach to highlight what it considers the achievements of the Tinubu administration and canvass support for his second term. The PDP chairman said the coalition was committed to expanding its mobilisation network across the state, adding that its target was to secure 300,000 votes for the President. He also challenged the All Progressives Congress, APC, to mobilise an additional 500,000 votes, bringing the combined target of both parties to 800,000 votes. “The Rainbow Coalition has pledged 300,000 votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Bayelsa State. We are tasking the APC to deliver 500,000 votes to bring the total number of votes for the APC to 800,000 out of the one million, one hundred and fifty thousand Permanent Voter Cards collected in the state,” Turnah said. He said the coalition would intensify its grassroots engagements across Bayelsa as preparations gather momentum for the 2027 general elections. items.title: Le ministre Bacary Sarr à l’écoute des prêcheurs de la presse sénégalaise
items.description: Le ministre de la Communication et des Relations avec les Institutions, Dr Bacary Sarr, a reçu en audience, ce mardi 10 novembre 2026, une délégation de l’Association des prêcheurs de la presse sénégalaise. Cette rencontre, selon le communiqué publié à cet effet, a été l’occasion pour les représentants de l’association de faire part de leurs préoccupations et de soumettre plusieurs propositions visant à renforcer leur présence et leur contribution dans le paysage médiatique national. Au cours des échanges, les prêcheurs ont notamment plaidé pour une meilleure ouverture de l’espace médiatique à leurs interventions et une reconnaissance institutionnelle de leur rôle. Ils ont également exprimé le besoin de bénéficier de formations en éthique et en déontologie, afin de renforcer leurs capacités et d’adapter leurs pratiques aux exigences du métier. Par ailleurs, la délégation a proposé la mise en place d’un cadre permanent de concertation avec les autorités. Une initiative qui permettrait, selon elle, de mieux structurer les échanges et de consolider leur contribution à l’éducation aux valeurs universelles ainsi qu’à la sensibilisation des populations. De son côté, le ministre Bacary Sarr a prêté une oreille attentive aux différentes préoccupations exprimées. Il a salué le rôle des prêcheurs et leur engagement dans la promotion des valeurs au sein de la société. Il les a également assurés de toute son attention pour un examen approfondi des attentes formulées. Cette audience ouvre ainsi la voie à un dialogue entre les autorités en charge de la communication et les acteurs du prêche dans les médias, autour des conditions de leur participation à l'espace médiatique.

items.title: Three feared killed as gunmen attack mining site in Plateau
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – No fewer than three persons have reportedly been killed following an attack by gunmen on a mining site in Jol community, Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident occurred at about 6pm on Tuesday, when the assailants reportedly stormed the mining site and opened fire on people in the area. A resident of the community, Bulus Shen, who confirmed the incident, told newsmen that the gunmen arrived at the mining site in the evening and began shooting sporadically. Shen said the attack threw the community into panic, adding that three persons were reportedly killed in the incident. The spokesperson of the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM), Rwang Tengwong, also confirmed the attack. Tengwong condemned the killing, describing the incident as disturbing and unacceptable. He called on security agencies to urgently investigate the attack, apprehend those responsible and strengthen security around rural communities to prevent further loss of lives. Efforts to get further details from security operatives were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Three feared killed as gunmen attack mining site in Plateau appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Musique : après 12 ans d’absence, Djessou Mama Diabaté signe son retour avec l’album « Koroya »
items.description: Après douze années d’absence sur la scène musicale, la chanteuse guinéenne Djessou Mama Diabaté prépare son retour avec un nouvel album intitulé « Koroya ». Composé de neuf titres, cet opus sera disponible le samedi 14 novembre 2026 sur les plateformes de streaming. L’artiste l’a présenté à la presse ce mardi 10 novembre, au Centre culturel franco-guinéen (CCFG), à Conakry. Forte de plus de 30 ans d’expérience dans la musique, Djessou Mama Diabaté entend mettre son vécu et son parcours au service de la transmission culturelle. Dans son intervention, l’artiste explique que « Koroya » est un album dans lequel elle partage son expérience et les enseignements tirés de la vie. « On est bébé, on grandit, mais on finit par vieillir. Et plus on considère que quand on vieillit, on devient plus sage », a-t-elle expliqué, présentant son œuvre comme une invitation à la responsabilité et à la transmission aux nouvelles générations. Prenant la parole, son manager, Fodé Bangaly Diabaté, a précisé que l’album a été enregistré en France, avec la participation du guitariste guinéen Moh Kouyaté, qui en a assuré la direction artistique et la réalisation musicale. La production est signée Caroline Thomas, à travers Folie Son Production. Sur le plan musical, « Koroya » propose un mélange de sonorités traditionnelles et modernes. L’album comprend notamment les titres « Sori » et « Kennebolo », ainsi que des reprises de classiques comme « Salimou ». L’artiste revisite également son titre emblématique « Konkobatati », dans une nouvelle version associant notamment le balafon, la guitare acoustique et le violoncelle. Concernant les perspectives, l’équipe annonce plusieurs rendez-vous sur scène. Djessou Mama Diabaté est notamment programmée le 15 décembre au Centre culturel franco-guinéen, dans le cadre du Salon de la musique guinéenne et des Victoires de la musique. Elle est également annoncée au festival Africolor, en France, pour deux dates, les 4 et 24 décembre. Malgré ses plus de 30 ans de carrière, Djessou Mama Diabaté déplore le manque de moyens financiers pour soutenir ses projets musicaux. Une situation qu’elle juge préoccupante au regard de son parcours. Elle a également plaidé pour une meilleure reconnaissance des griots, estimant que leur contribution à la préservation et à la transmission du patrimoine culturel mérite davantage de considération. Elle a, dans ce sens, interpellé les autorités sur la nécessité d’un accompagnement plus conséquent des artistes guinéens. Avec « Koroya », Djessou Mama Diabaté amorce ainsi une nouvelle étape de sa carrière, après douze ans loin de la scène musicale, avec l’ambition de faire connaître davantage la musique guinéenne au-delà des frontières.

items.title: Matoto : les téléphones portables désormais interdits dans les établissements scolaires
items.description: La Direction communale de l’éducation (DCE) de Matoto a décidé d’interdire l’utilisation des téléphones portables et des smartphones dans les établissements scolaires pendant les heures de cours. La mesure concerne aussi bien les élèves que les enseignants et le personnel d’encadrement. Dans une note de service signée par son directeur, Sékou Kaba, en date du 10 novembre 2026, la DCE de Matoto précise que cette interdiction s’applique dans les salles de classe, dans la cour de l’établissement ainsi que pendant les évaluations. La note instruit également chaque élève d’éteindre son téléphone et de le ranger dans son sac dès son arrivée dans l’établissement. Tout appareil utilisé en classe sera confisqué et remis à la Direction. Sa restitution ne pourra intervenir qu’en présence d’un parent ou d’un tuteur, après la signature d’un engagement. En cas de récidive, l’élève s’expose d’abord à un avertissement écrit, puis à une exclusion temporaire, conformément au règlement intérieur de l’établissement. Cette disposition concerne également les enseignants pendant leurs heures de cours. Toutefois, des exceptions restent possibles pour des raisons pédagogiques, à condition qu’elles soient préalablement autorisées par la Direction. Selon la note de service, la mesure entre en vigueur immédiatement et son strict respect est exigé de l’ensemble des acteurs concernés.

items.title: PM Shehbaz stresses clean energy’s importance for Pakistan at Chashma-5 nuclear plant event
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has emphasised that Chashma-5 (C-5) Nuclear Power Plant represents clean electricity and energy security for the people of Pakistan. The premier made the remarks, aired on Tuesday, at a ceremony marking the dome placement of the C-5 plant near Mianwali. The placement of a nuclear plant’s dome, which is weather-sealed, signifies the end of civil works and the beginning of internal construction and installation. A government press release hailed the progress as a “major milestone” for the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC). It noted that the C-5 project will have a generation capacity of 1,200 megawatts (MW) and is expected to commence electricity generation in September 2030. In his remarks, PM Shehbaz noted that while the structure may be a mix of concrete and steel, it represented “a promise of clean, reliable and affordable electricity”. He highlighted the advantages, saying it generated “power that does not rise and fall with the price of imported fuel; power that does not depend on whether the sun shines or the wind blows; and power that runs through the night” for factories and hospitals. He also observed that Pakistan, as a climate-vulnerable country, has a responsibility to pursue energy solutions that support economic goals while protecting the environment. “This project will turn dreams into hope and hope into reality one day soon,” the premier added. PM Shehbaz recalled that when he stood at the site in July 2023 during the groundbreaking ceremony, he had said that Pakistan “would not wait for anyone, but would build its own future through our hard work and untiring efforts”. “Today, less than three-and-a-half years later, the dome stands in place ahead of schedule,” the premier added, calling it a proud moment for the country and thanking engineers, technicians and workers from Pakistan and China who worked on the project. “I am confident that with the same commitment we will see this project commissioned ahead of time,” he remarked. Continuing his speech, he thanked Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir for his support in advancing Pakistan’s socio-economic development. The premier also extended his gratitude to China for its assistance in building C-5, Pakistan’s seventh nuclear plant that the neighbour helped build. “Each one stands as a living testament to a friendship that has never wavered, be it the wildest storms or fair weather,” PM Shehbaz said, thanking Chinese President Xi Jinping and his government. “Your engineers have worked shoulder-to-shoulder with ours, through summer heat and winter chill as one team,” he added. “The friendship between our two countries is often described as higher than the Himalayas, deeper than the oceans, sweeter than honey, more precious than gold and diamonds, and stronger than steel.” He extended congratulations to the China Atomic Energy Authority and PAEC, as well as gratitude to the people of Mianwali for hosting the plant. “Our defining role must be to harness every resource, every technology and every citizen to build the Pakistan that Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah had dreamt of: a Pakistan that is economically dominant, energy independent and environmentally resilient,” PM Shehbaz stated. According to PID, PAEC Chairman Dr Raja Ali Raza Anwar highlighted that nuclear power plays an important role in Pakistan’s energy security by providing reliable and low-carbon electricity. He added that Pakistan’s nuclear power plants safely and efficiently generate 3,530MW of electricity, avoiding 15 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually, the press release read. He further highlighted that nuclear energy accounted for around 16.6 per cent of the country’s electricity generation, despite representing only 8.6pc of its installed capacity, with its share of electricity generation rising to 26pc during winter.

items.title: Meurtre à la Marsa | Deux suspects arrêtés et placés en détention
items.description: Les services de la sous-direction des affaires criminelles relevant de la direction de la police judiciaire ont rapidement élucidé l'affaire du meurtre commis à Sidi Daoud, dans la circonscription de La Marsa, dont a été victime un jeune homme de nationalité camerounaise. Les éléments de l'enquête indiquent qu'une violente dispute a éclaté entre la victime et deux individus originaires de pays d'Afrique subsaharienne. L'altércation a rapidement dégénéré et la victime a été visée par plusieurs coups de couteau mortels, alors que les deux suspects ont pris la fuite. Alertées, les unités sécuritaires ont engagé des investigations qui ont permos d'identifier les suspects et une embuscade rigoureusement planifiée a permis de les arrêter au niveau de Bahr Lazreg, alors qu'ils étaient encore en possession de l'arme blanche ayant servi au crime. Les deux suspects ont été placés en détention sur ordre du ministère public alors que l'enquête se poursuit. Y. N. items.title: Abia 2027: Agbazuere makes U-turn, backs Otti’s 2nd term bid
items.description: . Dismisses Ogbonnaya’s alleged anti-Ngwa claim, warns critics By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—Former Chief of Staff to ex-Governor Okezie Ikpeazu, Prof. ACB Agbazuere, who strongly opposed Governor Alex Otti during the 2019 governorship election, has thrown his weight behind the governor’s re-election bid, declaring that he deserves a second term. Agbazuere, now a member of Otti’s Campaign Advisory Council, also dismissed allegations credited to former Commissioner, Chief Charles Ogbonnaya, that the governor allegedly described Ngwa people as brainless, describing the claim as unfounded and politically motivated. Speaking during a radio interview simulcast across several stations in Abia on Tuesday, Agbazuere warned politicians against making unsubstantiated allegations, saying defamatory statements could attract civil and criminal consequences under Nigerian laws, including the Cybercrimes Act. He said the allegation posed no threat to Otti’s political support base, particularly among the Ngwa people. “Dr Alex Otti may love peace; Dr Alex Otti may not want trouble, but they should see that people like us are now with him. Anybody who wants to say anything should be careful and say what he knows to be true,” he warned. Explaining his support for the governor, Agbazuere said Otti’s administration had demonstrated commitment to infrastructure development, urban renewal, workers’ welfare and good governance. He cited the reconstruction of Port Harcourt Road and Bank Road in Aba, the Omenuko Bridge and Arochukwu Road as evidence of the administration’s infrastructure drive. He also commended the governor for regular payment of salaries, pensions and gratuities, as well as improvements in traditional rulers’ allowances. On criticisms that increased federal allocations should have translated into more projects, Agbazuere argued that the rising cost of construction materials must be considered, citing the increase in cement prices from about N2,000 to N12,000 per bag. He challenged critics to visit the state and assess ongoing projects rather than judge the administration from a distance. Describing Otti as a banker and trained economist, he said the governor understood accountability and prudent management of public resources. Agbazuere urged Abians to look beyond party affiliations and support continuity, arguing that a second term would enable Otti to complete ongoing projects and consolidate his administration’s programmes. He recalled that even during the 2023 election, a leading opposition governorship candidate had reportedly acknowledged Otti as the best candidate. Vanguard reports that Agbazuere, a former Commissioner for Information, was among Otti’s vocal critics but recently switched allegiance after dumping the All Progressives Congress (APC), where he briefly sought political shelter shortly after Otti assumed office in 2023. He hails from the same Isiala Ngwa South Local Government Area with Gov. Otti. The post Abia 2027: Agbazuere makes U-turn, backs Otti’s 2nd term bid appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Economie Pastorale : Conakry accueille la première session du Comité régional de pilotage du PRADEP-AOS
items.description: La première session du Comité régional de pilotage du Programme régional d’appui au développement de l’économie pastorale en Afrique de l’Ouest et au Sahel (PRADEP-AOS) s’est ouverte ce mardi 10 novembre 2026 à Conakry. La cérémonie d’ouverture a été présidée par le ministre de l’Élevage, Alpha Bacar Barry, en présence de plusieurs personnalités, notamment des représentants du Comité permanent inter-États de lutte contre la sécheresse dans le Sahel (CILSS), de l’Union européenne, de l’agence belge de développement Enabel, de la CEDEAO, de l’UEMOA, des États bénéficiaires, des opérateurs de mise en œuvre et des organisations professionnelles pastorales. Prévue du 10 au 11 novembre 2026, cette première session intervient après le lancement officiel du programme, le 9 juillet 2026 à Lomé, au Togo. Doté d’un financement de 60 millions d’euros de l’Union européenne sur une durée de 60 mois, le PRADEP-AOS couvre 13 pays et vise à renforcer durablement l’économie pastorale dans la région, notamment à travers la gouvernance des ressources naturelles transfrontalières, la santé animale, le développement des chaînes de valeur et l’amélioration du cadre politique et réglementaire. À l’ouverture des travaux, le ministre Alpha Bacar Barry a rappelé l’importance de l’élevage dans les économies rurales et les moyens de subsistance des populations. Il a notamment évoqué les difficultés liées au changement climatique, à la pression foncière, à l’accès à l’eau et aux pâturages, aux maladies animales transfrontalières ainsi qu’aux conflits entre agriculteurs et éleveurs. Pour le ministre, ces défis nécessitent une réponse collective, mais également une meilleure prise en compte des pratiques traditionnelles dans la prévention des conflits liés à la mobilité pastorale. « Le code pastoral, ou je pourrais dire la tradition pastorale, précède nos États. Et c’est là où il faut aller chercher la solution », a-t-il déclaré. Abordant les actions envisagées par son département, Alpha Bacar Barry a indiqué que la sécurisation des espaces pastoraux, la prévention des conflits et le renforcement des infrastructures de production et de commercialisation du bétail représentent une part importante des investissements du ministère. Il a également annoncé l’aménagement prochain de couloirs de passage pour faciliter la traversée du bétail venant des pays limitrophes et favoriser la stabilisation des troupeaux. Prenant la parole au nom de la délégation de l’Union européenne, Gianpiero Borgillo a insisté sur la nécessité de préserver la dimension régionale du programme. Il a rappelé que les difficultés liées à la mobilité pastorale, aux ressources naturelles et aux marchés dépassent les frontières nationales et nécessitent des réponses concertées. « Le risque serait que, sous l’effet des contraintes de mise en œuvre ou des priorités nationales, le programme dérive vers une juxtaposition d’actions nationales sans cohérence d’ensemble », a-t-il averti. Il a ainsi appelé à une gouvernance claire, à une meilleure répartition des responsabilités entre les différents acteurs et à un dispositif de redevabilité permettant de mesurer les résultats obtenus. Il a également souligné que cette session doit contribuer à préciser les orientations du programme pour 2027, notamment sur la gestion concertée des contraintes liées à la mobilité pastorale et les contributions des différentes parties prenantes aux politiques pastorales. Au nom des opérateurs de mise en œuvre, le directeur pays de l’agence belge de développement Enabel en Guinée, Said Karmaoui, a réaffirmé leur engagement à accompagner les interventions du programme dans les différents couloirs. « Le programme ne sera véritablement régional que si les apprentissages circulent, si les outils essentiels sont compatibles et si les réponses tiennent compte des interactions entre territoires de départ, de transit et d’accueil », a-t-il indiqué. Il a identifié trois conditions essentielles à la réussite du programme : la qualité du dialogue avec les administrations et les organisations pastorales, une programmation réaliste tenant compte des capacités locales et de la durabilité des investissements, ainsi qu’une gouvernance lisible permettant d’éviter les chevauchements de responsabilités. De son côté, Abdoul Aziz Ag Alwaly, secrétaire général du Réseau Billital Maroobé (RBM), représentant des organisations professionnelles pastorales, a attiré l’attention sur les difficultés auxquelles sont confrontés les ménages pastoraux et agropastoraux dans la sous-région. Il a notamment cité les difficultés d’accès à l’eau et aux pâturages, les restrictions de mobilité, les déplacements anticipés des troupeaux, les tensions et les risques sanitaires. Il a estimé que ces contraintes doivent être prises en compte dans la planification des activités du programme, en adaptant les priorités, les calendriers et les moyens aux besoins des territoires de départ, de transit et d’accueil. « Nous attendons de ce comité une programmation 2027 réaliste, assortie de responsabilités claires et de moyens conséquents », a-t-il déclaré. Il a également plaidé pour une participation effective des organisations de la société civile aux décisions, avec une attention particulière à la place des femmes et des jeunes. Intervenant au nom du secrétaire exécutif du CILSS, le secrétaire exécutif adjoint, Dr Sylvain Nafiba Ouédraogo, a rappelé les objectifs du PRADEP-AOS et les principales étapes de sa mise en œuvre. Il a précisé que le programme entre désormais dans une phase opérationnelle, après la mise en place de son unité régionale de coordination, chargée d’assurer la coordination globale et le secrétariat du comité régional de pilotage. Concernant les travaux de cette première session, il a indiqué que les participants procéderont à l’examen du bilan des activités de 2026 et de leur niveau d’exécution dans les différentes composantes, avant d’examiner et de valider le plan de travail et le budget annuel 2027. Les échanges porteront également sur les synergies avec d’autres projets intervenant dans le secteur pastoral, notamment le PRAPS et le PEPISAO 2, ainsi que sur la présentation et l’adoption des outils communs de coordination, de suivi-évaluation, de rapportage, de capitalisation et de communication. À l’issue de la rencontre, les travaux devront aboutir à un rapport général, un document consolidé de planification pour 2027 et une matrice de synergie entre les différentes initiatives. Le responsable du CILSS a par ailleurs annoncé une formation destinée aux institutions focales territoriales, prévue du 12 au 14 novembre à Conakry. Elle portera notamment sur l’appropriation du programme et la maîtrise des outils développés par le Centre régional AGRHYMET, dont le géoportail, la bibliothèque numérique et les dispositifs de collecte de données par smartphone. Les travaux de cette première session du Comité régional de pilotage du PRADEP-AOS se poursuivent jusqu’au mercredi 11 novembre 2026.

items.title: Élections régionales 2026 en Guinée : La HAC annonce le tirage au sort pour le journal de campagne
items.description: Alors que la campagne électorale pour les élections régionales du 29 novembre 2026 est officiellement ouverte depuis hier lundi 9 novembre à 23h59, la Haute Autorité de la Communication (HAC) précise les modalités de participation des candidats à la couverture médiatique du scrutin. Dans un communiqué publié ce mardi 10 novembre 2026, l'organe de régulation annonce la tenue, ce mercredi 11 novembre à 10 heures, de la cérémonie de tirage au sort destinée à déterminer l'ordre de passage des candidats dans le journal de campagne. Selon la HAC, cette opération se déroulera au siège des stations de la Radio rurale ainsi que dans les locaux des radios privées partenaires de l'institution. Elle concerne les candidats des communes urbaines et rurales désireux de prendre part à la campagne médiatique. L'institution insiste toutefois sur une condition de participation. « Seuls les candidats présents lors du tirage au sort seront pris en charge dans la programmation », précise le communiqué. Pour rappel, la campagne électorale des régionales, prévue sur toute l'étendue du territoire national, a débuté le 9 novembre à 23h59 et prendra fin le jeudi 26 novembre 2026 à 23h59, soit trois jours avant le scrutin.

items.title: Obuasi SHTS sexual abuse probe 85% complete; evidence points to prosecution – Education Minister
items.description: The Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, says investigations into the sexual abuse allegations involving female students of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) are 85 per cent complete, with evidence gathered so far pointing to a prima facie case for prosecution. He said the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of the Ghana Police Service was handling the criminal aspects of the case, while a committee established by the government on October 14 was nearing the completion of its investigations. Mr Iddrisu disclosed this when he addressed Parliament on Tuesday, November 10, after appearing before the joint parliamentary committees on Human Rights, Gender and Education to brief them on developments in the case. “Mr. Speaker, I’m happy to note and report that the Criminal Investigation Department of the Police Service is dealing with the criminal aspects of it, which has to do with sexual assault against some students at Obuasi Technical,” he told the House. He added that the committee established on October 14 had made significant progress and that the evidence gathered could support prosecution. “Mr Speaker, I’m happy to know that a committee we put together on the 14th of October is 85% complete with its investigation, and the weight of evidence suggests that a court would have considered the matter that a prima facie case is established against for purposes of prosecution that we expect to start shortly,” he said. The Minister’s update comes amid growing public concern over allegations of sexual abuse involving the school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, and female students. The allegations gained national attention following a JoyNews investigation by investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni, titled Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow , which detailed claims of sexual harassment, assault and rape involving students. The investigation reported that complaints had been made to school management and education officials months before the headmaster was interdicted. ‘ It also cited accounts from students, parents and teachers who said concerns about the alleged abuse had not received adequate attention. The Ghana Education Service (GES) subsequently interdicted Mr Abdulai on October 14 to facilitate investigations, while the Education Minister referred the criminal aspects of the allegations to the police. The case has also attracted scrutiny over the handling of earlier complaints. A committee that investigated disturbances at the school in August 2026 reported that the sexual harassment allegations presented to it were not substantiated by the evidence available at the time. However, that inquiry was separate from the fresh investigations initiated after the JoyNews exposé. The police have also investigated a rape complaint filed by a student on August 4, 2026, and forwarded the case docket to the Attorney-General for study and advice. Police clarified that the docket concerned that particular complaint, while other allegations would require separate investigations.
