2027: Avoid technicalities, treat electronic evidence rigorously, INEC charges tribunals
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Professor Joash Amupitan SAN, has urged members of the 2027 Election Petition Tribunals to avoid technicalities that defeat substantive justice and to subject electronic evidence to rigorous scrutiny. He also told them to keep firm control of their courtrooms and let “truth of the ballot prevail”. According to the commission’s Daily Bulletin of Tuesday, Amupitan spoke on Monday in Abuja while delivering the Commission’s opening remarks at a three-day workshop for Justices of the Court of Appeal and members of the tribunals, held at the Body of Benchers Complex. The Court of Appeal organised the workshop under the theme “Election Tribunal as a Tool for Political Stability.” The INEC chairman said electoral litigation had grown more complex, with disputes now touching on voter accreditation, electronic transmission of results, technological failures and the integrity of digital records. On the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System BVAS and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), he said technology should neither be treated as infallible nor dismissed simply because the evidence is electronic. Amupitan warned that digital disinformation driven by artificial intelligence, audio cloning and deepfake videos would inevitably spill into the courtrooms. He urged the tribunals to apply strict evidentiary standards under Section 84 of the Evidence Act, saying digital provenance, forensic chain of custody and reliance on certified data from INEC would be vital to stop synthetic fabrications from misleading the courts. He added that electoral adjudication is evidence-driven, and that allegations of irregularities, non-compliance or result manipulation must be proved with credible and legally admissible evidence. According to him, the Commission has issued the Regulations and Guidelines for the Conduct of Elections, 2026, to give clearer operational standards against which claims of non-compliance can be weighed in proceedings. The INEC chairman told the tribunal members that they carry the democratic aspirations of over 200 million Nigerians once they take their oaths. He described the courtroom as the altar on which public confidence in constitutional governance is preserved, and urged them to let their decisions reflect deep fidelity to the law, uncompromising integrity and the principle that justice must be seen to be done. Amupitan said Nigeria’s political stability in 2027 would depend not only on how efficiently INEC conducts elections, but also on how courageously, transparently and justly the tribunals settle the disputes that follow. He described the Election Petition Tribunal as a constitutional valve that releases political pressure and keeps electoral friction from degenerating into civil disruption. A tribunal that acts with procedural speed, evidentiary rigour and absolute impartiality, he said, assures aggrieved parties that a credible platform exists to assess their complaints on merit. The workshop, he noted, was taking place at a pivotal point in the country’s democratic journey. The Presidential and National Assembly elections hold on January 16, 2027, followed by the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6, 2027. Amupitan said the legitimacy of the country’s constitutional democracy rests on two pillars: impartial electoral administration and fearless judicial adjudication. He added that no institution can secure electoral integrity alone, since credible elections need an impartial electoral management body, responsible political parties, informed citizens, professional security agencies and an independent, effective judiciary. He commended the Court of Appeal, the National Judicial Institute and the legal experts behind the Second Edition of the Judicial Electoral Manual (JEM), 2026, calling it an indispensable compass for consistency in judicial reasoning. Conflicting decisions on similar facts, he said, create legal uncertainty and erode public confidence. The INEC chairman stressed that engagement between the Commission and the Judiciary must stay within constitutional limits and must never become a channel for influencing judicial decisions or discussing the merits of pending cases. He assured the Judiciary that INEC respects those boundaries and remains committed to complying with valid judicial decisions. The event featured the swearing-in of the chairmen and members of the 2027 tribunals, and the unveiling of the Second Edition of the manual by the Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat M. O. Kekere-Ekun. The President of the Court of Appeal, Justice M. B. Dongban-Mensem, disclosed that 375 judicial officers had been nominated to serve on the tribunals, made up of 138 returning members with previous tribunal experience and 237 newly nominated members. She urged the nominees to stay steadfast in judicial independence, resist every form of improper influence and discourage unnecessary adjournments, stressing that speed must never come at the expense of fairness. The post 2027: Avoid technicalities, treat electronic evidence rigorously, INEC charges tribunals appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Makinde presents N1.12trn final budget
items.description: …Allocates 60% to capital expenditure …Dismisses appointees’ resignations as meaningless By Adeola Badru Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, on Tuesday presented a proposed N1.12 trillion budget for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly, describing it as the “Budget of Sustained Progress”, while dismissing the recent resignations of political appointees as inconsequential. Makinde said the departure of some officials from his administration would not distract his government or affect its commitment to delivering its mandate. The governor made the remarks while presenting the 2027 Appropriation Bill, valued at N1,115,341,378,359.94, before lawmakers at the Parliament Building, Secretariat, Ibadan. Speaking against the backdrop of recent resignations by political appointees and other government officials, Makinde said he was keeping count of those who had left but insisted that their decisions were of no significance to his administration. He also disclosed that one of the female officials who resigned had approached him with what he described as an impossible request, adding that she tendered her resignation after he declined to grant it. The presentation is particularly significant as the proposed estimates represent the final appropriation bill of Makinde’s administration, which is expected to complete its second term in 2027. Under the proposal, capital expenditure accounts for N670.03 billion, representing 60.07 per cent of the total budget, while recurrent expenditure stands at N445.31 billion, or 39.93 per cent. Explaining the allocation, the governor said the proposed spending reflected his administration’s determination to sustain infrastructure development, consolidate existing achievements and strengthen the delivery of essential services across the state. He said about 60 per cent of every N100 provided for in the budget would go into capital investments, stressing that infrastructure remained central to economic growth and long-term prosperity. Makinde, however, cautioned that physical infrastructure alone could not guarantee meaningful development without adequate investment in human resources and essential public services. He said schools needed teachers, hospitals required healthcare professionals, medicines and equipment, while public institutions must be adequately staffed and equipped to function effectively. According to him, the proposed budget was also informed by consultations with stakeholders and residents across the state’s administrative and political zones, whose concerns and expectations shaped the government’s spending priorities. The governor also used the occasion to advocate continuity in governance beyond the expiration of his tenure, unveiling what he called the Omituntun 3.0 agenda. He said the initiative was designed to prevent a reversal of the development trajectory established by his administration over the past seven and a half years after the 2027 governorship election. Makinde said: “Over the last seven-plus years, we have worked towards sustaining the development trajectory of Oyo State. For the candidates we have recommended for continuity, we refer to this agenda as Omituntun 3.0. “While political parties may contest elections and some may emerge victorious while others lose, our overriding concern is to ensure that the development of the state does not suffer a setback. “For the continued development of Oyo State in 2027 and beyond, I will place this agenda before the Governor, while the incoming administration will also be expected to take it forward from where we stop.” The proposed 2027 budget represents an increase over the original 2026 appropriation of N891.99 billion, which allocated N502.85 billion, representing 56.37 per cent, to capital expenditure and N389.14 billion, or 43.63 per cent, to recurrent spending. However, following the approval of a N210 billion supplementary budget by the State House of Assembly in September 2026, the state’s total financial provision for the 2026 fiscal year rose to N1.102 trillion. Meanwhile, Speaker of the Oyo State House of Assembly, Adebo Edward Ogundoyin, described the presentation of the 2027 budget as a significant milestone in the state’s democratic and developmental journey, being the final budget cycle of the Makinde administration. Ogundoyin said the occasion offered an opportunity to consolidate the achievements of the past seven and a half years, sustain ongoing programmes and strengthen the foundation for sustainable growth. He recalled that the first budget of the Omituntun 2.0 administration was presented before the Assembly on December 5, 2023, describing the latest presentation as another important moment in the relationship between the Executive and Legislative Arms of Government. The Speaker said the state had witnessed considerable developments in infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and security under the present administration. He listed investments in road construction and rehabilitation, school infrastructure, healthcare facilities, agricultural development and workers’ welfare as efforts aimed at repositioning the state for sustainable development. Ogundoyin disclosed that the 10th Assembly, since its inauguration in June 2023, had passed 41 bills into law, processed 146 committee reports and 184 motions, and adopted more than 1,500 resolutions on issues affecting the welfare, security and development of residents. He said the Assembly had also strengthened participatory lawmaking through public hearings and stakeholder engagements, adding that it had organised 11 major public hearings and stakeholder meetings within the period. Among the legislative proposals and policy issues considered, he listed the Oyo State Real Properties Protection Bill, Presumptive Tax Bill, Consumer Protection Agency Bill, Oyo State Roads Fund Bill and Single-Use Plastics Prohibition Bill. He added that the Assembly had engaged stakeholders on market administration, cooperative societies, public safety and the remuneration of political and public office holders. The Speaker identified the establishment of a Post-Legislative Scrutiny (PLS) Unit in January 2025 as one of the major institutional achievements of the 10th Assembly. He described the Oyo legislature as the first State House of Assembly in Nigeria to establish a dedicated unit for the exercise. According to him, the unit had scrutinised the Oyo State Open Rearing and Grazing Regulation Law, 2019, and the Oyo State Security Network Agency Law, 2020, to assess their implementation, identify challenges and recommend improvements. Ogundoyin said recommendations from the scrutiny of the Open Rearing and Grazing Regulation Law had informed the progress of its amendment bill, which had passed second reading in the Assembly. He also disclosed that a post-legislative scrutiny inquiry had commenced on the Oyo State Sexual and Gender-Based Response Agency and Referral Law. On security, the Speaker said the Assembly had organised a security summit that brought together relevant stakeholders to examine the state’s security situation and develop practical responses to emerging challenges. He maintained that the legislature had continued to discharge its constitutional oversight responsibilities beyond the passage of appropriation bills, with a commitment to transparency, accountability and prudent management of public resources. Ogundoyin assured the governor that the House would subject the proposed 2027 budget to thorough legislative scrutiny, guided by the interests of residents. He said the estimates should consolidate existing achievements, prioritise the completion of ongoing projects and address critical developmental needs across the state. The Speaker also appealed to Makinde to address welfare concerns raised by the Parliamentary Staff Association of Nigeria (PASAN), Oyo State Chapter. The requests, he said, included an upward review of the Consolidated Legislative Salary Structure (CONLESS) to 100 per cent, regularisation of ad-hoc staff appointments and the release of a bus earlier approved for the association. He said addressing the demands would improve staff welfare, strengthen institutional capacity, enhance productivity and sustain industrial harmony within the Legislative Arm. On the 2027 general elections, Ogundoyin expressed confidence that residents would support candidates of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), citing what he described as the administration’s record in governance, infrastructure and people-centred policies. He also expressed optimism that an incoming APM administration would implement the proposed 2027 budget and complete the projects and programmes contained in it. Earlier, lawmakers representing constituencies across the state commended Makinde’s administration, describing its leadership as visionary, inclusive and people-oriented. They highlighted what they considered achievements in infrastructure, education, healthcare and residents’ welfare since the administration assumed office in 2019. The lawmakers particularly praised the administration’s investment in Ladoke Akintola University of Technology (LAUTECH), describing the acquisition of sole ownership of the institution by the Oyo State Government as a landmark achievement in the education sector. Some also commended the governor’s approach to appointments, saying his emphasis on merit had created opportunities for people without established political connections to occupy positions of responsibility. items.title: Déploiement de l’armée algérienne au Niger : l’UE corrige sa position
items.description: L’Union européenne fait machine arrière et corrige sa position sur le déploiement d’unités de l’armée algérienne au Niger. Elle a affirmé ce mardi respecter « pleinement » la souveraineté de l'Algérie et du Niger, et ce après avoir demandé, le 30 octobre dernier via son porte-parole Anouar El Anouni, aux deux pays des « éclaircissements » sur la décision de déployer des unités de l’ANP dans ce pays du Sahel. Ce mardi, le même porte-parole a souligné que cette décision de l’Algérie relevait « exclusivement » des relations bilatérales entre les deux pays, selon le compte-rendu de l’agence APS. Le porte-parole de l'UE pour les Affaires étrangères et la politique de sécurité Anouar El Anouni a indiqué que son ambassadeur de l'UE en Algérie et de son chargé d'affaires au Niger ont été évoqués par Alger et Niamey. Il a expliqué que ces démarches « relevaient des pratiques établies par la Convention de Vienne sur les relations diplomatiques ». Algérie – Niger : l’UE « n’a aucune volonté d’ingérence » L'UE « n'a aucune volonté d'ingérence » dans les affaires de l’Algérie et du Niger, précisant « n'avoir à aucun moment eu l'intention de demander à Alger ou à Niamey des clarifications sur leur engagement bilatéral », a ajouté Anouar El Anouni. Le gouvernement nigérien a annoncé que le Premier ministre, Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine a convoqué le chargé d’affaires par intérim de la délégation de l’Union européenne (UE) à Niamey pour « exiger des clarifications » à propos des déclarations « inacceptables et condescendantes » d'un porte-parole de l’UE pour les affaires étrangères, concernant les relations entre l’Algérie et le Niger. En Algérie, l’agence APS a recadré le porte-parole de l’UE pour ses déclarations et accusé Paris « d’acharnement » contre l’Algérie. items.title: IPOB accuses Britain of complicity in Kanu’s rendition
items.description: By Steve Oko The Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) has accused the British government of complicity in the alleged persecution of its detained leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, particularly his abduction in Kenya and extraordinary rendition to Nigeria. The group also accused Britain of maintaining diplomatic silence over what it described as persistent violations of Kanu’s fundamental rights, despite his British citizenship. IPOB made the allegations in a statement issued by its Media and Publicity Secretary, Comrade Emma Powerful, following recent interventions by Bishop Godfrey Onah on historical injustices associated with Nigeria’s colonial experience and the treatment of the South-East. The pro-Biafra group said Britain’s historical involvement in Nigeria’s political and economic affairs had contributed to what it described as structural injustices against Biafra and its people. It alleged that Britain’s failure to intervene over Kanu’s rendition, its response to calls for his release and what it described as the disregard of previous appellate court decisions reflected a continuation of colonial-era policies that prioritised strategic interests over justice. IPOB also accused the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) and other Western media organisations of promoting what it described as an anti-Kanu narrative. It claimed that online searches for Kanu’s name predominantly returned negative reports, alleging that such coverage had contributed to what it called a distorted international perception of his agitation and the circumstances surrounding his prosecution. The group further alleged that Kanu’s transfer to a prison in Sokoto was politically motivated, claiming it was an attempt by the All Progressives Congress-led Federal Government to use his detention as a political bargaining tool to secure support in the North ahead of future elections. It, however, claimed that the alleged political calculation had backfired and cautioned against using Northern Nigerians as instruments in what it described as divisive political manoeuvring. On Kanu’s trial, IPOB faulted the characterisation of its leader as someone who hates the North, insisting that his agitation was directed against what it called a corrupt neo-colonial political structure, rather than any ethnic or religious group. The group specifically challenged a remark attributed to Justice Omotosho that Kanu hated the North with a passion, describing it as a distortion of his broadcasts and political message. According to IPOB, Kanu’s struggle is against a system it alleges exploits the resources and sacrifices of ordinary Nigerians for the benefit of the political elite. It maintained that Bishop Onah’s intervention reflected growing recognition of the historical grievances of Biafrans and the need to address the issues underlying the agitation. The group insisted that what it described as media manipulation and judicial and political manoeuvring would not derail its campaign for the peaceful emancipation of Biafra. IPOB called on the British government to break its silence and take a more decisive position on Kanu’s case, arguing that its alleged inaction, despite his British citizenship, raised questions about its commitment to protecting the rights of its citizens abroad. items.title: Ouagadougou : Plus de 41 700 poussins de chair saisis par la Direction des services vétérinaires
items.description: La Direction générale des services vétérinaires, avec l’appui de la Gendarmerie nationale, a procédé, ce lundi 9 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, à la saisie de plus de 41 700 poussins de chair introduits frauduleusement sur le territoire national. Ces poussins, destinés à la production de viande, ont été acheminés au Burkina Faso en violation des mesures d’interdiction prises par le ministère de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques. À travers un communiqué, le ministère avait pourtant invité les opérateurs économiques à mettre fin à cette pratique. « Malgré cette interdiction, certains contrevenants continuent de s’adonner à l’importation frauduleuse de poussins de chair », a déploré Dr Kadré SANFO, Directeur de la santé publique vétérinaire et de la législation. Il a rappelé que la production nationale dispose de capacités suffisantes pour couvrir les besoins du marché. « Les capacités nationales ont été évaluées et les services restent mobilisés pour accompagner les acteurs afin de satisfaire la demande », a-t-il assuré. À la suite de cette saisie, des analyses de laboratoire sont en cours afin de vérifier l’état sanitaire des poussins et de s’assurer qu’ils ne sont porteurs d’aucune maladie. Une telle mesure vise à prévenir toute contamination du cheptel national et la propagation d’éventuelles maladies aviaires. Dr Kadré SANFO a également invité les populations à faire preuve de vigilance. Il a souligné que les poussins introduits frauduleusement échappent aux contrôles sanitaires et au dispositif de suivi vétérinaire. Leur acquisition expose ainsi les éleveurs à des risques importants, notamment l’achat de sujets de mauvaise qualité, susceptibles de compromettre leurs investissements. À l’inverse, les poussins issus de la production nationale bénéficient de prélèvements et de contrôles réguliers auprès des accouveurs. Ces opérations permettent de vérifier leur état sanitaire et de garantir leur qualité. Le Directeur de la santé publique vétérinaire et de la législation a lancé un appel à la responsabilité de l’ensemble des acteurs. S’adressant aux éleveurs, il les a exhortés à s’approvisionner exclusivement auprès des établissements agréés, régulièrement suivis par les services vétérinaires et offrant des garanties sur la qualité sanitaire des poussins. Les commerçants, quant à eux, doivent se rapprocher des accouveurs nationaux afin de nouer des partenariats pour assurer un approvisionnement régulier des éleveurs en poussins de qualité. Il a enfin invité les populations à signaler aux services compétents tout cas suspect d’importation frauduleuse de poussins. Pour Dr Kadré SANFO, la lutte contre l’importation frauduleuse constitue un enjeu majeur de protection du cheptel national, mais aussi de préservation des investissements et de promotion de la filière avicole nationale. Les poussins de mauvaise qualité peuvent en effet fragiliser les exploitations et décourager les initiatives d’investissement dans le secteur. 𝗗𝗖𝗥𝗣/𝗠𝗔𝗘𝗥𝗔𝗛 Minute.bf

items.title: Carex Rewards Thousands Of Consumers As Everybody Wins Promo Concludes With Grand Finale Live Draw
items.description: Carex, one of Nigeria’s leading personal hygiene brands, has successfully concluded its nationwide Everybody Wins Promo with a transparent Grand Finale Live Draw, rewarding loyal consumers and reinforcing its commitment to delivering value beyond personal care products. The campaign, which ran from June 2026 to August 2026, attracted millions of consumers PAN Nigeria and rewarded winners with prizes worth over ₦400,000,000. The Grand Finale Live Draw, held in Lagos, brought together consumers, media representatives, trade partners, regulatory officials, and other key stakeholders to witness the selection of the campaign’s grand prize winner through a transparent and independently supervised process. The event marked the culmination of months of consumer participation and engagement, further strengthening the connection between the Carex brand and its consumers. Throughout the promotion, participants had multiple opportunities to win exciting rewards, including instant Recharge Cards, shopping Vouchers, and a brand-new Car. Over 90,000 consumers emerged as winners over the course of the campaign. The grand prize car winner, Faith Stephen from Ijebu Ode, Ogun State, emerged through the live draw process conducted in accordance with all applicable promotional and regulatory requirements. Speaking at the event, Ifunanya Anwunah, Head of Category – Personal Hygiene, said: “At Carex, we believe that the consumers who trust our products every day deserve to be appreciated and rewarded. The Everybody Wins Promo was created as a tangible expression of our gratitude for the loyalty and support we continue to receive from Nigerian families. The overwhelming participation and enthusiasm witnessed throughout this campaign demonstrate the strong connection consumers have with the Carex brand. The promo was built on a simple promise: giving everyday consumers the opportunity to win meaningful rewards while enjoying the quality, care, and protection they have come to trust from Carex. As a brand trusted by millions of Nigerians for their personal hygiene and care needs, Carex remains committed to developing initiatives that deepen consumer engagement, reward loyalty, and create memorable experiences for consumers across the country. items.title: Second Pakistan-Sri Lanka Test shifted from Lahore to Rawalpindi over smog
items.description: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Tuesday shifted the second Test between Pakistan and Sri Lanka from Lahore to Rawalpindi amid worsening smog conditions in the Punjab capital. According to an official announcement issued by the PCB, the match, originally scheduled to be played in Lahore from November 17 to 21, will now take place at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on the same dates. “The second Test match between Pakistan and Sri Lanka, originally scheduled to be played in Lahore from November 17 to 21, has been relocated to Rawalpindi due to prevailing weather conditions,” PCB spokesperson Amir Mir said in a post on X. He said the decision was taken in view of increasing smog levels in Lahore and concerns over deteriorating air quality. It may be mentioned that Lahore has been grappling with severe smog for the past 10 days, with the city’s Air Quality Index (AQI) reportedly touching 600 , placing it among the world’s most polluted cities. The venue change means both Tests of the two-match series will now be played at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. The first Test is currently under way at the same venue. Pakistan declared their first innings at 434 for nine on the second day, with Saud Shakeel top-scoring with 93. Sri Lanka were 114 for three in their second innings when bad light stopped play. Sri Lanka have been touring Pakistan since early October. Pakistan won the three-match T20I series 2-1 before claiming the ODI tri-series, which also featured England. The ongoing Test series is part of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27 cycle.

Mr Ablakwa acknowledged Mr Olson’s contribution to strengthening relations between Ghana and the United States, particularly in the areas of education and security. items.title: A policy born out of sight, not sympathy: Ghana’s new dawn for persons with disabilities
items.description: The launch of the Free Tertiary Education for Persons with Disabilities Initiative by His Excellency John Dramani Mahama has ignited renewed hope and pride among Ghana’s disability community. Beyond promises, this policy marks a visionary step; one that recognizes ability over disability and sets Ghana on course to become a continental model of inclusive development. A POLICY OF SIGHT: SEEING ABILITY OVER DISABILITY For many years, the refrain among persons with disabilities in Ghana has been one of hope mixed with uncertainty, hope for recognition, inclusion and empowerment, as well as uncertainty about when that hope would materialize into real systemic change. Today, that narrative is being rewritten. The announcement by His Excellency John Dramani Mahama, President of the Republic of Ghana, during the launch of the Free Tertiary Education for Persons with Disabilities Initiative, at the Accra College of Education on Friday, 24 th October, 2025 has rekindled an unprecedented sense of optimism, dignity, and a sense of belonging among the disability community. This bold vision marks a memorable turning point in our nation’s moral and social consciousness; one that views disability not through the lens of sympathy, but through the lens of sight, fairness, and capability. A VISION ROOTED IN EMPOWERMENT AND EQUITY What makes this initiative exceptional is not merely its content, but its philosophy. For the first time in Ghana’s policy history, disability inclusion is being pursued not as an act of charity, but as a strategic national development goal. The initiative recognizes that disability should not prevent a qualified Ghanaian from pursuing a university degree, Higher National Diploma (HND) or diploma. It seeks to make tertiary education more accessible to persons with disabilities who are most often excluded as a result of financial circumstances. The policy provides for the payment of eligible beneficiary’s academic and residential fees in all public tertiary institutions as part of the support package. From the passage of the Persons with Disabilities Act 2006, Act 715, to the allocation of portions of the District Assemblies Common Fund (DACF) to persons living with disabilities, and to the creation of Disability Health and Resource Centres across second-cycle and public tertiary inclusive institutions in Ghana, this is a comprehensive national vision grounded in equity, empowerment, and opportunity. The President’s directives have sent a clear message: Persons with disabilities are not liabilities to be pitied, but assets to be developed and celebrated. His emphasis on transforming our national mindset “from commiseration to partnership, from exclusion to empowerment, and from antagonism to solidarity” has resonated deeply within the hearts and minds of all Ghanaians who believe in justice and inclusion. COMPLETING THE CIRCLE OF INCLUSIVITY In the spirit of compassion, fairness, and nation-building, it is timely to make one heartfelt appeal; to extend the “Free Tertiary Education for PWDs Policy” to graduate persons with disabilities. The pursuit of higher education beyond the undergraduate level is a critical step for persons with disabilities to be fully equipped to contribute at the highest levels of governance, leadership, and national development. While free tertiary education will open doors to countless young persons with disabilities, many graduates continue to face financial and structural barriers as they pursue postgraduate degrees or professional certifications. By expanding this special intervention to cover graduate-level studies , persons with disabilities will not be left behind in policy, administration, and leadership roles where graduate qualifications are most often a requirement. Furthermore, Ghana will complete the circle of inclusivity His Excellency has so admirably begun. A further and compelling justification for extending this special initiative to postgraduate education is the employment reality confronting many persons with disabilities after graduation. Currently, too many PWDs who successfully complete tertiary education still struggle to secure employment in spite of their qualifications and capabilities. For some, an undergraduate degree does not provide a sufficient competitive advantage in an increasingly demanding labour market, where advanced qualifications, specialist knowledge, and professional credentials can influence access to meaningful employment and leadership opportunities. Without targeted support to pursue further studies, many capable graduates with disabilities risk remaining unemployed or being excluded from positions for which they could otherwise be well qualified. Extending the policy to cover postgraduate and other relevant graduate-level programmes would therefore help remove a major financial barrier and enable eligible PWDs strengthen their expertise, broaden their career prospects, and compete more effectively for employment. In the long term, this investment could also help position more persons with disabilities to contribute meaningfully to policy formulation, implementation, and evaluation, as well as to public administration, institutional leadership, research, and national development. The policy should not merely help PWDs enter tertiary institutions; it should also help create pathways for them to progress, lead, and participate in shaping the decisions that directly affect their lives and the future of Ghana. Such a move would not only enhance access but would also position Ghana as a continental leader; a nation where education becomes the ultimate tool of liberation for all citizens, regardless of physical condition. It would demonstrate that our compassion is matched by courage, and our vision by conviction. A CALL TO COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY The President has rightfully called upon the private sector, civil society, universities, and the media to join in this noble vision. Disability inclusion cannot be the work of government alone; it must be a shared national mission. Let us, therefore, as a people, take the bull by the horn and ensure that this transformative policy becomes a living and breathing testament of Ghana’s moral strength and developmental maturity. In conclusion, this new chapter in Ghana’s disability rights movement reminds us that true progress is not measured by sympathy, but by systems; not by handouts, but by opportunities; and not by rhetoric, but by results. Indeed, we are witnessing a policy born of sight, not sympathy. A sight that sees beyond physical limitations to the vast potential that lies within every Ghanaian. And as we move forward together as persons with, and those without disabilities, we reaffirm a shared truth: when inclusion becomes the norm, development becomes unstoppable. Author Bio Isaac Ansah is the Ghana Gas Disability Liaison Officer, as well as the Senior Community Relations and CSR Officer for the Community Relations Division of Ghana National Gas Ltd Company, where he advocates for inclusive development and disability empowerment. His work focuses on corporate social responsibility, inclusive education, and livelihood empowerment programmes for persons with disabilities. #JohnMahamaDisabilityLegacies #InclusionIsNationBuilding #AbilityOverDisability #EducationForAll

items.title: Hassan Ayariga acknowledges government’s economic gains but questions impact on living standards
items.description: Founder and Leader of the All People’s Congress (APC), Dr Hassan Ayariga, has acknowledged improvements in Ghana’s macroeconomic performance under the National Democratic Congress (NDC) government in 2026 but says the gains must translate into better living conditions for ordinary Ghanaians. In an assessment of the government’s performance ahead of the 2027 Budget presentation, Dr Ayariga cited progress in fiscal consolidation, inflation reduction and revenue mobilisation. He noted that the Bank of Ghana had reported a decline in the fiscal deficit for the first half of 2026 compared with the corresponding period in 2025, alongside a primary fiscal surplus. He also acknowledged that inflation had fallen substantially from the high levels recorded in previous years. However, he cautioned that lower inflation does not necessarily mean prices have fallen or household incomes have improved. He said the government must demonstrate how economic stabilisation is translating into stronger purchasing power, better wages, employment and business opportunities. Dr Ayariga also raised concerns about government expenditure, citing Bank of Ghana reporting that total expenditure in the first half of 2026 was approximately 24.9 per cent below its programmed target. Capital expenditure was also below the programmed level, raising questions about the timely release of funds to ministries, departments and agencies. He said the shortfall could affect the implementation of programmes in critical sectors, including healthcare, education, agriculture, road construction and water infrastructure. While cautioning that the expenditure gap does not automatically establish that the Finance Minister personally refused to release funds, he called on the Ministry of Finance to publish a comprehensive report detailing the amounts allocated, released and spent by each ministry during the year. Dr Ayariga said the 2027 Budget must provide clear answers on funding shortfalls and how the government intends to improve implementation of approved programmes. He further urged the government to prioritise productive employment, Ghanaian enterprise development, infrastructure, agricultural productivity and public financial accountability. The APC leader said the success of government should ultimately be measured by improvements in the welfare of citizens, rather than budget announcements and macroeconomic indicators alone. His assessment, dated November 10, 2026, comes ahead of the government’s presentation of the 2027 National Budget to Parliament on Thursday, November 12.

items.title: «Stature présidentielle» : dans un sondage, Marine Le Pen creuse l’écart avec ses concurrents
items.description: La septieme « vague » du barometre Verian sur la stature presidentielle des candidats potentiels, realisee pour Le Figaro Magazine et publiee ce 10 novembre, confirme la position dominante de Marine Le Pen dans les sondages en vue de la presidentielle de 2027. Dans cette etude, 43 % des personnes interrogees ont estime que la candidate du Rassemblement national (RN) possedait « les competences pour etre une bonne presidente », soit cinq points de plus en un mois. edouard Philippe arrive deuxieme (31 %) et Bruno Retailleau ferme le podium avec 23 % de « oui ». La deputee du Pas-de-Calais a egalement progresse de sept points sur la « vision claire de l'avenir de la France » (46 %) et de quatre points sur la capacite « de prendre les decisions necessaires » au pays (43 %). Quant a savoir si elle « represente bien la France et les Francais », la cheffe de file des deputes RN a l'Assemblee nationale voit sa cote progresser de 2 points, a 44 %. Sur ces trois criteres, son avance sur edouard Philippe et Bruno Retailleau, qui conservent respectivement les deuxieme et troisieme places, est encore plus nette que sur le premier. Bruno Retailleau talonne par David Lisnard La dynamique dont jouit Marine Le Pen semble toutefois inegale selon les generations. Ainsi, seuls 22 % des 18-24 ans jugeraient Marine Le Pen capable de prendre les decisions dont le pays a besoin, contre 50 % chez les 25-34 ans. Sur la question des competences presidentielles, l'ecart est egalement marque : 33 % chez les plus jeunes, contre 48 % dans la tranche d'âge superieure. Enseignement notable de ce barometre Verian : l'arrivee de David Lisnard. Le maire de Cannes et president de l'Association des maires de France recueille entre 22 % et 24 % d'opinions positives selon les quatre criteres evalues. Des resultats proches de ceux du president des Republicains et candidat a la fonction supreme, Bruno Retailleau (23 % a 24 %), avec lequel il est habituellement compare. Fait notable : David Lisnard devance l'ancien Premier ministre macroniste Gabriel Attal sur l'ensemble des indicateurs (21 % a 22 %), mais reste toutefois derriere un autre Premier ministre de l'ere Macron egalement candidat : edouard Philippe, credite de 28 % a 31 %. David Lisnard beneficie notamment d'une meilleure appreciation a droite (31 % a 35 %) et a « l'extreme droite » (39 % a 41 %), tandis que ses scores sont nettement plus faibles au centre (15 % a 19 %). Sa notoriete reste neanmoins un obstacle pour l'heure : entre 37 % et 38 % des personnes interrogees declarent ne pas savoir evaluer la stature presidentielle de ce nouvel arrivant dans les sondages, soit pres de trois fois plus que pour les autres candidats etudies.

items.title: ADC-PCC to Tinubu: Where is the electricity you promised Nigerians?
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for his unfulfilled electricity pledge, accusing him of resorting to personal attacks, divisive rhetoric and recycled promises instead of presenting a credible scorecard of his administration. The Council said Nigerians expected the President to explain what had become of his major campaign promises after nearly three-and-a-half years in office, particularly against the backdrop of worsening insecurity, widespread hunger, rising living costs and massive government borrowings. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC said Tinubu’s recent campaign outings in Kaduna, Rivers and Jigawa states offered little beyond verbal attacks on opponents and familiar promises. Recalling the President’s electricity pledge, the Council challenged him to explain why millions of Nigerians were still struggling with unreliable power supply. “If I don’t give you electricity, don’t vote for me for a second term,” it quoted Tinubu as saying. The ADC-PCC described his renewed electricity promises during the Jigawa campaign as an attempt to repackage an old commitment, adding that the President had reportedly invested in alternative power arrangements for his personal comfort. The Council also questioned the fate of 2,000 tractors reportedly imported from Brazil under the administration’s mechanised farming initiative, alleging that they had yet to make any meaningful impact on agricultural productivity. It further accused Tinubu of taking credit for projects initiated by his predecessor, late President Muhammadu Buhari, insisting that his administration had little of its own to showcase. On the state of democracy, the ADC-PCC accused the President of undermining the independence of democratic institutions, alleging undue influence over the National Assembly and attempts to compromise the Judiciary. It also took issue with Tinubu’s declaration that ‘all is fair in politics’. warning that such a position could encourage political illegality, intimidation, violence and thuggery. The Council said: “The opposition is increasingly confronted with unconstitutional conduct, judicial rascality, political intimidation and a compromised electoral environment under the APC administration.” Citing the President’s recent campaign outing in Rivers State, the ADC-PCC questioned his decision to praise and promise to reward a political figure whom it alleged had been illegally removed from office, denied political participation for six months and prevented from seeking re-election. “Reward him for what?” Ologbondiyan queried, describing the President’s conduct as an affront to constitutional governance and the democratic rights of the people. The Council accused Tinubu of deploying divisive rhetoric whenever confronted with questions about his administration’s performance, rather than providing verifiable answers to Nigerians. It maintained that the country needed leadership anchored on accountability, competence, transparency and respect for democratic institutions. items.title: Minerals Commission CEO calls for prosecution of Chinese nationals involved in illegal mining
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Minerals Commission, Isaac Andrews Tandoh, has called for the strict enforcement of Ghana’s mining laws against Chinese nationals and companies involved in illegal mining, saying foreign investors must be held accountable regardless of their nationality. Speaking at the China-Ghana Mining Cooperation Conference 2026, Mr Tandoh said Ghana’s mining regulations applied equally to all operators and that no foreign national or investor should be shielded from sanctions for breaking the law. He said a proposed framework agreement between Ghana and China was expected to strengthen cooperation in enforcing mining regulations and prosecuting Chinese nationals found engaging in illegal activities. “Under the new framework agreement we are doing with the Chinese government, they are supporting us to go ahead and prosecute Chinese who find themselves on the wrong side of the law. They will go through the sanctions, and when they go back, Chinese law will also take care of them,” he said. The conference brought together stakeholders in Ghana’s mining industry, including the President of the Ghana Chamber of Mines, Ing. Frederick Attakumah, and China’s Ambassador to Ghana, H.E. Cong Song. Mr Tandoh said Ghana remained open to foreign investment in its mineral resources but insisted that all investors must operate within the country’s legal and regulatory framework. His comments come amid continuing concerns about illegal small-scale mining, popularly known as galamsey, which has contributed to the degradation of water bodies, farmlands and other natural resources. China’s Ambassador to Ghana, H.E. Cong Song, called for a balanced approach to mining cooperation, cautioning against using Africa’s natural resources as instruments of geopolitical rivalry. He said the continent’s mineral wealth should instead support economic transformation, sustainable development and mutually beneficial international partnerships. “Africa’s resources should not be used for political rivalry,” he said. Mr Cong also emphasised the need for mutual respect and cooperation, as well as recognition of African countries’ development priorities in decisions concerning the management and use of their natural resources. A major highlight of the conference was the unveiling of the China-Ghana Mining Talent Development Centre (CMTDC), an initiative aimed at strengthening technical skills, knowledge exchange and technology transfer in Ghana’s mining industry. The centre is expected to serve as a training and capacity-building hub for Ghanaian workers and mining professionals, offering opportunities to acquire specialised technical expertise and industry-related skills. Its proposed programmes are also expected to support the development of local capabilities and contribute to the modernisation of the mining sector. The initiative forms part of broader efforts to deepen Ghana-China mining cooperation while increasing Ghanaian participation across the mining value chain. The partnership’s impact, however, will depend on its ability to deliver tangible benefits in areas such as responsible mining, environmental protection, technology transfer and skills development.

items.title: Patoranking reunites with Olamide for new Lagos-inspired single, ‘Welcome to Lagos’
items.description: Nigerian reggae and dancehall star Patoranking has teamed up with rapper Olamide on a new single titled ‘Welcome To Lagos’, celebrating the energy, ambition and cultural influence of Nigeria’s commercial capital. Released on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, through Amari Musiq, the collaboration brings together two prominent Nigerian music acts on a record inspired by the city’s vibrant lifestyle, nightlife and cultural identity. Produced by longtime Patoranking collaborator Ctea, the song combines rolling basslines, syncopated drums and a chant-driven hook, with Patoranking’s signature blend of Afrobeats, reggae and dancehall. Olamide complements the record with a verse that pays homage to Lagos, referencing the city’s traditional praise name and celebrating the place both musicians call home. An official music video directed by UAX was also released alongside the single. The filmmaker previously worked with Patoranking on the visuals for ‘African Soldier’, his collaboration with Jamaican reggae and dancehall star Buju Banton. ‘Welcome To Lagos’ is the fourth single from Patoranking’s forthcoming fifth studio album, following earlier releases including ‘No Jonze’, ‘African Soldier’ featuring Buju Banton and ‘Shake That’ featuring Ruger. The collaboration also comes ahead of Olamide’s 13th studio album, Time & Space , scheduled for release on November 16, 2026. It follows his announcement of a headline performance at London’s O2 Arena on March 25, 2027. Patoranking rounds off eventful year with new collaboration The release comes after a busy year for Patoranking, marked by international performances, award recognition and activities beyond music. The singer recently completed a summer festival run across the UK and Europe, performing at events including Africa Oye, Summerjam, Sunsplash and Reggae Geel. In September, he returned to Lagos for a headline performance at TRACE Live, where he celebrated 10 years of his debut album, God Over Everything , originally released in 2016. That same month, he won Best Male Reggae/Dancehall at the 2026 African Muzik Magazine Awards (AFRIMMA) in Dallas, Texas. His collaboration with Ruger, ‘Shake That’, was also nominated for Best Collaboration. In October, Patoranking headlined the Nigerian Independence Day Parade in New York and received the Philanthropy Impact Award from the Nigerian Consulate in New York and the Organization for the Advancement of Nigerians (OAN), recognising his philanthropic contributions. Beyond his music career, the artiste has supported youth development and education through initiatives including the ALU Patoranking Scholarship, which provides fully funded educational opportunities to students across Africa. A decade of global music success Born Patrick Nnaemeka Okorie on May 27, 1990, in Ebute Metta, Lagos, Patoranking rose to prominence with his breakout single ‘Girlie O’ and went on to establish an international following through songs such as ‘My Woman, My Everything’ and ‘Abule’. His discography includes God Over Everything (2016), Wilmer (2019), Three (2020) and World Best (2023). His 2023 album featured collaborations with international and African acts including Ludacris, Beenie Man, Popcaan, Diamond Platnumz, Victony and Kizz Daniel. With more than 800 million YouTube views and hundreds of millions of streams reported across digital platforms, Patoranking has built a career that connects Afrobeats, reggae and dancehall audiences across different markets. ‘Welcome To Lagos’ adds another collaboration to his catalogue while bringing together two Nigerian artistes to celebrate the city that has played a significant role in shaping their musical journeys. The single and its accompanying music video are available across digital music platforms. Listen to ‘Welcome To Lagos’ here .

items.title: Douentza et Koro : le retour des déplacés confronté à d’importants défis
items.description: Apres plusieurs annees de deplacement, les habitants de Drimbe, dans le cercle de Douentza, amorcent les preparatifs de leur retour. Ils se mobilisent pour deblayer leur village, abandonne depuis pres de huit ans. Dans le cercle de Koro, plusieurs localites ont deja accueilli une partie de leurs habitants. Toutefois, l'acces a l'eau potable, la reconstruction des habitations et les conditions de securite restent des defis majeurs. a Drimbe, dans le cercle de Douentza, des centaines d'habitants se sont mobilises mardi et jeudi derniers pour deblayer leur village, abandonne depuis pres de huit ans. Accompagnes notamment du chef de village et du chef de cercle de Douentza, ils ont entrepris de couper les arbres et de degager les voies envahies par la vegetation afin de faciliter le retour des populations. Selon le chef du village, Nouh Ousmane, cette initiative fait suite a plusieurs rencontres entre les habitants et les autorites locales et administratives de Douentza. « Tout ce que nous voulons, c'est rentrer chez nous. Nous avons rencontre les autorites pour leur faire part de notre volonte de retourner au bercail. Elles nous ont assure etre disposees a nous accompagner », confie le chef du village qui ajoute cependant qu'il y a destravaux a faire. « Nos anciennes habitations sont envahies par les arbres et doivent etre entierement nettoyees. Cela pourrait prendre trois mois. Toutes les constructions se sont effondrees », explique-t-il. Un besoin d'appui materiel Au-dela de la volonte de rentrer chez eux, les habitants de Drimbe sont confrontes a l'ampleur des travaux de nettoyage. Arsike Tamboura et Mariam Maïga soulignent l'importance des besoins et appellent a un accompagnement materiel, notamment pour couper les arbres et degager les voies d'acces. Pour Arsike Tamboura, le travail engage est particulierement difficile et necessite des moyens adaptes. « Le travail n'est pas facile. Ce n'est pas quelque chose qui peut etre termine en peu de temps. Nous avons besoin de materiel pour nettoyer toute la localite. Il n'y a pratiquement que des arbres sur place et il faut les couper », martele Arsike Tamboura. Apres cette etape,poursuit-elle , « nous pourrons identifier les autres besoins et solliciter des appuis supplementaires. Nous avons deja commence a recevoir de l'aide ». De son cote, Mariam Maïga insiste sur la necessite de rendre les habitations de nouveau accessibles et habitables. « Nous ne pouvons pas envisager de rentrer tant que nos habitations restent dans cet etat, sales et inhabitables. Nous demandons de l'aide a tous », lance-t-elle. L'eau potable et la securite, des priorites Le deblayage n'est pas le seul defi auquel les habitants de Drimbe doivent faire face. D'autres infrastructures essentielles sont necessaires pour rendre leur retour possible et durable. Le chef du village, Nouh Ousmane, indique qu'un château d'eau a deja ete installe, mais que les autres points d'approvisionnement en eau sont hors d'usage. Il appelle egalement a la consolidation de la securite et au renforcement de la cohabitation pacifique avec les communautes voisines. « C'est la paix que nous souhaitons avant tout. Il n'y a actuellement qu'un seul château d'eau, tandis que tous les puits sont bouches. Nous demandons a chacun de nous apporter son soutien. Notre souhait est de vivre en parfaite harmonie avec les autres communautes et de continuer a nous frequenter comme auparavant », affirme-t-il. Dans le cercle de Koro, l'acces a l'eau reste preoccupant Pendant ce temps, dans le cercle de Koro, plusieurs localites ont deja enregistre le retour d'une partie de leurs habitants. C'est notamment le cas de Youdiou, Guerou, Kombougourou et Anakarawa, dans la region de Bandiagara. Mais ces retours s'accompagnent de nombreuses difficultes. Les populations sont notamment confrontees au manque d'eau potable et a la destruction des habitations. Selon Aly Kole Bolly, conseiller du chef de village d'Anakarawa, l'acces a l'eau et la reconstruction des maisons figurent parmi les besoins les plus urgents. « Actuellement, notre seule preoccupation est d'avoir de l'eau potable. Ici, il n'y a ni eau ni habitations. Nous sommes revenus nous installer, mais nous sommes confrontes au manque d'eau. C'est ce dont nous avons le plus besoin », temoigne-t-il. a Drimbe comme dans plusieurs localites du cercle de Koro, le retour des populations deplacees marque une etape importante vers la reprise de la vie communautaire. Cependant, entre le deblayage des villages, l'acces a l'eau potable, la reconstruction des habitations et les imperatifs de securite, les defis restent nombreux. Pour ces populations, il ne s'agit pas seulement de rentrer chez elles, mais aussi de pouvoir y vivre dans des conditions dignes et durables. items.title: Govt slashes petrol price by Rs8 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs7 in another reduction
items.description: The government on Tuesday slashed the price of petrol by Rs8 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs7. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs338 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs371 on Nov 11 (Wednesday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra). The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end. On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation. The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc. The government and Jamaat-i-Islami held another round of negotiations today to formulate a way forward on relief in petroleum prices. Rise in fuel prices The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months. Since July 17 , the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: L’entourage de Vladimir Poutine œuvre à prolonger sa vie
items.description: Aujourd’hui, mardi 10 novembre, le président de l’Institut Kourtchatov et proche allié de Poutine, Mikhaïl Kovaltchouk, a déclaré lors d’un forum sur la génomique organisé à Moscou que ses équipes de chercheurs menaient des études sur des primates afin de trouver des moyens pour allonger la vie humaine en bonne santé – un sujet auquel Vladimir Poutine s’intéresse de près Ковальчук допустил создание регуляторной системы для продления жизни человека », Tass , 10 novembre 2026.'> 1 . En septembre 2025, lors d’un échange capté par un micro à Pékin, le président russe avait déclaré à son homologue chinois Xi Jinping : « Avec le développement des biotechnologies, les organes humains peuvent être continuellement transplantés. Les gens peuvent vivre de plus en plus vieux et même atteindre l’immortalité ». Xi lui avait alors répondu : « Les prédictions disent qu’au cours de notre siècle, il y a des chances qu’on vive jusqu’à 150 ans ». Mikhaïl Kovaltchouk est un proche conseiller officieux du dirigeant russe sur les questions scientifiques, notamment celles liées à la génétique. Son frère, le milliardaire Iouri Kovaltchouk, est quant à lui considéré comme le « banquier personnel » de Poutine, avec qui il entretient des liens étroits au moins depuis les années 1990. Poutine a fêté en octobre son 74e anniversaire, ce qui fait de lui le plus âgé des dirigeants exerçant le pouvoir exécutif en Europe. Il dépasse ainsi de 6 ans l’espérance de vie à la naissance d’un homme en Russie, qui était de 68 ans en 2023, selon Rosstat. La fille aînée de Poutine, Maria Vorontsova, endocrinologue et directrice de l’institut médical de l’université d’État de Moscou, s’intéresse elle aussi à l’allongement de la durée de vie. Lors d’un forum organisé à Moscou en octobre, elle a déclaré que l’allongement de la vie ne devait pas reposer sur les seuls médecins, mais sur une culture de la santé inculquée dès l’enfance К обеспечению здорового долголетия предложили привлекать не только медиков », Vedomosti , 19 octobre 2026.'> 2 . Le gouvernement russe s’est fixé pour objectif de porter l’espérance de vie à 78 ans d’ici 2030, et à 81 ans d’ici 2036, dans le cadre d’un projet national intitulé « Vie longue et active » (« Продолжительная и активная жизнь »). Or, la guerre menée par le Kremlin en Ukraine depuis 2022 pèse lourdement sur la mortalité. Au premier semestre 2025, elle était responsable d’environ deux tiers des décès d’hommes âgés de 18 à 29 ans Hacked Records Show 400,000 Russians Killed in War on Ukraine », Bloomberg , 8 novembre 2026.'> 3 . Selon des données de Rosstat obtenues par le groupe biélorusse d’opposition Cyber Partisans et le collectif de hackers ukrainiens Silent Crow, environ 400 000 combattants russes seraient morts en Ukraine entre février 2022 et fin août 2026 Боевые потери России по данным Росстата , Silent Crow [Consulté le 10 novembre 2026].'> 4 . Ce chiffre est cohérent avec celui de l’État-major des forces armées ukrainiennes, qui a recensé 1,6 million de tués et de blessés graves : environ un sur quatre serait mort, une proportion proche des estimations occidentales. Rapportées à la population, ces pertes frappent surtout la Sibérie et l’Extrême-Orient : en Transbaïkalie, près d’un habitant sur 80 serait mort à la guerre depuis 2022, soit 18 fois plus qu’à Moscou. L’article L’entourage de Vladimir Poutine œuvre à prolonger sa vie est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Drame de Lompoul : Serigne Ahmadou Badawi Mbacké plaide pour la valorisation de la jeunesse
items.description: Le drame survenu au large de Lompoul, dans le département de Kébémer, qui a coûté la vie à 39 jeunes, a suscité une réaction de Serigne Ahmadou Badawi Mbacké, fils de Serigne Fallou Mbacké. S'exprimant en marge de la réunion du Comité local de développement (CLD) consacrée aux préparatifs du Magal de Kazu Rajab, ce mardi 10 novembre 2026, le guide religieux a rappelé l'importance de la jeunesse, qu'il considère comme une véritable richesse pour le Sénégal. La première réunion consacrée aux préparatifs du Magal de Kazu Rajab, prévu en janvier 2027, s'est tenue ce mardi 10 novembre 2026. Prenant la parole à cette occasion, Serigne Ahmadou Badawi Mbacké est revenu sur le drame survenu au large de Lompoul, dans lequel 39 jeunes, qui tentaient de rejoindre l'Europe par voie maritime, ont perdu la vie. Le guide religieux a présenté ses condoléances aux familles des victimes avant de prier pour le repos éternel de leurs âmes. Saisissant cette occasion, le fils de Serigne Fallou Mbacké a insisté sur la place fondamentale de la jeunesse dans le développement du Sénégal. Il a déploré de voir cette frange importante de la population prendre les pirogues dans l'espoir de rallier l'Europe. A lire aussi : Magal Kazu Rajab : Serigne Abo Mbacké remercie l’État et prêche l’exemplarité de Serigne Fallou Mbacké « La jeunesse est la richesse la plus précieuse pour le Sénégal », a déclaré le guide religieux. Il a estimé que les jeunes doivent bénéficier d'une bonne éducation et d'une formation adéquate, mais également être portés par l'espoir afin de les encourager à rester dans leur pays et à contribuer à son développement. Rappelant que 75 % de la population sénégalaise a moins de 30 ans, Serigne Ahmadou Badawi Mbacké a souligné l'importance de ce potentiel démographique. « N'importe quel pays rêverait d'avoir cette frange importante de la population », a-t-il fait remarquer. Il a enfin formulé des prières pour que cessent les départs vers l'Europe par voie maritime. Birane DIOP, correspondant

items.title: Insuffisance rénale au Sénégal : Plus de 750 000 Sénégalais concernés, 4000 nouveaux cas graves chaque année
items.description: Au Sénégal, l'insuffisance rénale est un véritable défi de santé publique. La prévalence est estimée à 4,9 %, soit plus de 750 000 personnes touchées, un chiffre lui-même sous-estimé. Ces statistiques sont du directeur général des établissements de Santé, Dr. Fallou Niang, qui s’est exprimé ainsi, lors de sa prise de parole, à l’occasion de l’inauguration du tout premier centre d’hémodialyse dans le département de Tivaouane, le 4 Novembre dernier, à l’hôpital Mame Abdou Aziz Sy Dabakh. Selon les estimations nationales, entre 2 000 et 4 000 personnes atteignent, chaque année, le stade avancé de la maladie rénale chronique, nécessitant un traitement de suppléance rénale : hémodialyse, dialyse péritonéale ou transplantation rénale. Venu représenté le ministère de la santé et l’hygiène publique, Dr. Niang a rappelé la vision de l'État, celle de la proximité et de gratuité de la prise en charge de la maladie. Pour le ministère, l'ouverture de ce centre à Tivaouane, en partenariat avec la Fondation Amal du Maroc, Carrefour Médical et le ministère chargé de la solidarité constitue une étape historique. « Cette infrastructure permettra non seulement d'augmenter massivement notre capacité de prise en charge nationale, mais elle s'inscrit surtout dans la politique de décentralisation des soins spécialisés », a souligné recteur général des établissements de santé. Il s'agit ainsi de rapprocher les soins des populations pour garantir l'équité territoriale et la dignité de chaque patient », a-t-il soutenu. Le représentant du ministre a rappelé que cette vision est consacrée par la constitution sénégalaise, notamment en son article 8 qui dispose que l'État et les collectivités territoriales garantissent des soins de santé de qualité, particulièrement pour les populations vivant en zone rurale. « La santé n'est pas un luxe, c'est un droit », a-t-il martelé. Le directeur général a également salué l'engagement du directeur de l'hôpital et de son personnel. Il a annoncé que sur instruction des plus hautes autorités, une grille d'évaluation de la qualité, centrée sur le patient et la satisfaction des usagers, sera déployée dans tous les établissements de santé. « La qualité des soins fait désormais partie des indicateurs de performance de nos établissements », a-t-il précisé. Le gouvernement du Sénégal, à travers le ministère de la Santé et de l'Hygiène publique, entend poursuivre ses investissements pour atteindre les objectifs de la couverture sanitaire universelle, conformément à l'axe 2 de l'Agenda national de transformation Sénégal Vision 2050. Celui-ci consacre, en effet, l'équité sociale et le capital humain. Cette vision passe par le renforcement des centres de dialyse pour asseoir une véritable souveraineté sanitaire et la promotion de la production locale d'intrants, à l'image de l'usine de carrefour médical à Diass, mais surtout, par le maintien de la gratuité de la dialyse, instaurée depuis 2012. « Nous continuerons à œuvrer avec nos partenaires techniques et financiers et la bénédiction de nos familles religieuses pour une amélioration continue de la santé de nos populations », a-t-il conclu. Le centre d'hémodialyse de l'hôpital Mame Abdou Aziz Dabakh, à terme, aura une capacité de 54 patients », a indiqué le directeur général des Établissements de Santé. Ibrahma NDIAYE ( Correspondant )

items.title: N210trn not missing from NNPC – Mele Kyari tells Senate
items.description: By Henry Umoru – ABUJA The immediate past Group Chief Executive Officer, GCEO, of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company, NNPC, Limited, Mele Kyari has appeared before the Senate, refuting alleged unaccounted N210 trillion in the balance sheet of the National oil company as contained in the 2017 to 2023 Audit report. Kyari who finally appeared before the Senator Ibrahim Dankwabo (PDP, Gombe North) led Senate Committee on Public Accounts said the alleged unaccounted figures arose from accounting entries which have nothing to do with financial loss. He declared that no such financial infraction happened under him as Chief Executive of NNPCL from 2019 to 2025. Kyari said, “I wish to confirm that nothing was lost. It is simply not possible that such an amount could have been lost under my care and leadership. “The matter relates to accounting entries, which have nothing to do with any financial loss. “They are bookkeeping issues, and I believe the appropriate explanations have been provided in my report.” The former NNPCL boss who declared that the N5billion allegedly spent on change of name from NNPC to NNPCL , waa untrue as there was no spending like that under his watch, however refuted queries raised in the audit report on registration and incorporation of NNPC Ltd. He said: “At the time of incorporation, the company was not owned by the Federation in the same manner. “The Federation was therefore responsible for the payment relating to the incorporation of NNPC. “However, NNPC made the payment on behalf of the Federation and subsequently charged it to the Federation’s revenue, which was reflected in what we referred to as the former NAPIMS account of NNPC. “This was simply an accounting entry, involving approximately N2.99 billion. It was a payment made to government institutions responsible for providing the relevant services. “I have also seen comments suggesting that N5 billion was paid for the naming of the company. That is not correct”. According to him, NNPCL under him was transformed from loss incurring corporation to a profit making company, adding that prior to his assumption of office as Group Managing Director of NNPC in 2019 , the national oil company had a huge loss of $803billion in 2018 operational year , which gradually turned to o profit making under him from 2019 . Kyari said, “Mr Chairman, you may be aware from the financial records that the company recorded a loss of about $803billion in 2018. “I took over in 2019, and we did everything possible to transform the company into a profitable organisation which made it to for the first time in its 44 years of existence, recording sustained profits” Satisfied with the submissions of Kyari , the Committee through its Chairman, Senator Dankwabo said , responses submitted to the queries shall be thoroughly studied for final decision on the audit report . Dankwabo said, ” we shall interrogate the figures submitted by the former GMD to know whether to Invite him again or not . ” For now , he has responded to the two issues relating to his leadership of NNPC during the period under review.” Vanguard News The post N210trn not missing from NNPC – Mele Kyari tells Senate appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sédhiou : ouverture de la 3ᵉ édition de la foire régionale
items.description: Pendant une semaine, la capitale du Pakao va abriter la troisième édition de la foire commerciale et agricole. Cet événement majeur est une occasion pour les agriculteurs, éleveurs et commerçants d'échanger leurs produits tout en dévoilant leur savoir-faire. Sédhiou abrite, depuis ce mardi 10 novembre, la 3ᵉ édition de la foire régionale. À la place de l'Indépendance, les stands d'agriculteurs, d'éleveurs et de commerçants rivalisent de produits. Cet événement est placé sous le thème : « Entreprendre, innover et investir pour un développement économique durable ». « Cette édition ambitionne de faire de notre région un territoire plus attractif, porté par le dynamisme de ses acteurs économiques, et elle valorise ses importantes potentialités », a d’emblée déclaré Ba Ousmane Danfakha, adjoint au gouverneur de la région de Sédhiou. De son côté, Ousseynou Diagne, secrétaire général de la chambre de commerce de Sédhiou, a précisé que « cette foire a été organisée pour mettre en relation toute la chaîne de valeur des produits qui existent dans la région de Sédhiou ». C'est un avantage, dit-il, pour les commerçants, acheteurs, agriculteurs et éleveurs, pour qu’ils puissent échanger sur leurs produits et voir comment réfléchir à la transformation et renforcer le développement de la région. La région de Sédhiou dispose d’atouts considérables dans le domaine de l’agriculture, de l’élevage, de la pêche continentale, de l’artisanat, du commerce et des services. C'est pourquoi, a ajouté le représentant du chef de l'administration territoriale, « transformer davantage ces potentialités en richesse, en emplois décents, en opportunités économiques pour nos populations, particulièrement les jeunes et les femmes, sont des défis qui nous interpellent ». A lire aussi : Les organisateurs veulent promouvoir la filière lait Cette édition dépasse le cadre d'une simple exposition commerciale. Selon Ba Ousmane Danfakha, elle constitue une véritable plateforme de rencontre, de partenariat d’affaires, de partage d’expérience et de promotion de l’investissement. Pour cette 3ᵉ édition, la filière élevage est à l’honneur. « L’objectif est aussi de montrer que la réussite de l’élevage est possible dans la région », a souligné Ousseynou Diagne, secrétaire général de la chambre de commerce, rappelant les avantages que présente Sédhiou pour la culture fourragère. Pour cette édition, la République sœur de Guinée-Bissau est l'invitée d’honneur. « Cette présence témoigne d'une volonté de coopération et d’ouverture sous-régionale », a assuré Ba Ousmane Danfakha, réaffirmant l’engagement de l’administration territoriale à accompagner les initiatives qui concourent au développement économique et social de notre région. La foire va se dérouler du 8 novembre au 14 du même mois. Cet agenda n’est pas fortuit ; il permet de mettre en avant la Journée nationale de l’élevage qui sera célébrée cette année à Sédhiou. Jonas Souloubany BASSENE (Correspondant)

items.title: ACF crisis deepens as chairman alleges invasion of secretariat
items.description: — Osuman accuses individuals of breaking into Kaduna headquarters, removing valuables By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The leadership crisis in the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) has taken a fresh turn following allegations by its National Chairman, Maman Mike Osuman, that some individuals forcibly gained access to the organisation’s national secretariat in Kaduna and removed valuables. In a petition dated November 9, 2026, and addressed to Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State, Osuman accused two individuals of allegedly breaking into the ACF headquarters at No. 11A Sokoto Road, Kaduna, without the authorisation of the recognised leadership. The petition was also copied to the Inspector-General of Police, the Kaduna State Commissioner of Police and the Director of the Department of State Services (DSS) in the state. According to Osuman, the individuals allegedly gained access to the premises by breaking the gates and office doors, changing the locks and removing valuables and other properties belonging to the organisation. He further alleged that the operation was carried out without the knowledge or consent of the recognised leadership of the forum and without a search warrant. Describing the alleged incident as an assault on the institutional integrity of the organisation, Osuman appealed to Governor Sani to intervene to prevent further escalation of the crisis. “An invasion of this nature not only violates the sanctity of our corporate headquarters but is also a direct assault on the dignity of the entire Northern Region,” he said. The chairman described the national secretariat as the collective heritage of Northern Nigeria, stressing that its protection was essential to preserving the dignity and integrity of the organisation. He urged the governor to use his good offices to ensure that the rule of law prevailed and that the forum was protected against actions capable of undermining its stability. The latest allegation has renewed attention on the protracted leadership crisis within the ACF, particularly the disagreement over control of its national secretariat and the authority to manage the organisation’s affairs. The dispute has been characterised by competing positions among the forum’s leadership organs over the interpretation of its constitution, leadership structure and the legitimacy of decisions taken by the contending sides. In one of the major developments, the National Executive Committee (NEC) of the forum reportedly suspended its Board of Trustees (BoT) Chairman, Alhaji Bashir M. Dalhatu, over alleged violations of the organisation’s constitution. The suspension followed an emergency NEC meeting held in Kaduna in May 2026, amid tensions over access to the ACF headquarters and reports of police restrictions ahead of the meeting. However, the Board of Trustees subsequently rejected Dalhatu’s purported suspension, describing the decision as illegal and unconstitutional and an attempt to destabilise the northern socio-cultural organisation. The opposing positions have exposed deep divisions within the forum, with stakeholders holding conflicting views over the interpretation of its constitution and the respective powers of its governing organs. The latest allegations surrounding the secretariat have further heightened concerns over the prolonged dispute and its implications for the unity and credibility of an organisation established to articulate the collective interests of Northern Nigeria. The post ACF crisis deepens as chairman alleges invasion of secretariat appeared first on Vanguard News .
