items.title: ADC-PCC to Tsoho: Explain why you transferred our case to Lifu
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has challenged the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, Justice John Tsoho, to explain why he transferred a case from Justice Emeka Nwite to Justice Peter Lifu barely 24 hours after receiving the party’s formal protest against the reassignment. The campaign council said the sequence of events raised serious questions about the handling of the case, particularly as Justice Nwite had already commenced hearing it and had neither recused himself nor ceased to be a serving judge. It demanded the immediate release of the full judgment, saying the failure to provide an official copy was obstructing the party’s right to challenge the decision at the Court of Appeal. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Phrank Shaibu, on November 10, the ADC-PCC said its lawyers had submitted the legal questions to the appellate court but insisted that Nigerians deserved to know how the case was transferred to Justice Lifu despite the party’s formal objection. The campaign council disclosed that the plaintiff had sought the transfer from Justice Nwite, citing delays and loss of confidence in obtaining a timely hearing. However, it said its counsel, in a response dated May 11, 2026, challenged the plaintiff’s account of the adjournments, outlined the circumstances surrounding the delays and described the application as an attempt at forum shopping. On June 2, the ADC National Secretary, Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola, also wrote to Justice Tsoho, asking him to reverse the reassignment and formally protesting the transfer on grounds of the party’s lack of confidence in Justice Lifu’s impartiality. The following day, the case was assigned to Justice Lifu. Questioning the decision, Shaibu said: “Justice Tsoho received our protest. Why did he proceed with the transfer? What did he find in the plaintiff’s allegation of delay that outweighed the court record and our protest? Let him publish his reasons. Let Nigerians read them beside the letters.” The campaign council said the Chief Judge owed Nigerians an explanation for disregarding the protest, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the transfer had created an appearance of possible bias. It also cited Justice Lifu’s earlier decision in a separate suit, in which he ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to deregister the ADC and four other political parties despite an existing Court of Appeal order staying proceedings. According to the ADC-PCC, the appellate court subsequently nullified the deregistration judgment, describing Justice Lifu’s decision to proceed with the matter as the ‘highest form of judicial impertinence’ and invoking Supreme Court authority on ‘judicial rascality’. The council further cited a certified judgment delivered by Justice Musa Liman, who dismissed a challenge to the ADC leadership for lack of merit and locus standi. It said Justice Liman had held that the internal party dispute was non-justiciable, declared the leadership handover lawful and affirmed INEC’s entitlement to recognise the party’s National Chairman and National Secretary. The ADC-PCC maintained that the judgment raised important legal questions about the subsequent proceedings before Justice Lifu, which its lawyers had placed before the Court of Appeal. The campaign council also called on the National Judicial Council (NJC) to investigate the reassignment, the formal protest submitted to the Chief Judge and Justice Lifu’s handling of the earlier deregistration case. Invoking Nigeria’s political history, it warned judicial officers against decisions capable of deepening political crises, recalling the controversies surrounding the judiciary before the collapse of the First and Second Republics. Turning its attention to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), the ADC-PCC challenged the party to confront its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, on the political field rather than resort to alleged judicial manoeuvres. “The hallowed chambers of our courts must not be turned into arenas for political combat. Nigerians must see those who would rather fight their opponent through court manoeuvres than meet him at the ballot box. “Atiku remains our candidate. The law is on his side, not sentiment. We will defend that position before the Court of Appeal and keep the record before Nigerians. Their right to choose their president must never become a bargaining chip in anyone’s struggle for power,” Shaibu added. items.title: We’ll defeat Nigeria’s enemies, Tinubu declares in Jigawa
items.description: ….President has won enemies of democracy – Yari By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: President Bola Tinubu has vowed to defeat those he described as enemies of Nigeria’s unity and stability, telling supporters at his ruling All Progressives Congress APC presidential campaign rally in Dutse, the Jigawa State capital, that the fight against insecurity will be won. Speaking on Tuesday, the President acknowledged the security worries of his audience. “I know you have problems of insecurity in Nigeria, but working together, see your neighbour as your friend and partner. See the individual, exchange information, anything you know about insecurity, report it immediately. We have been through many wars. We will defeat our enemies. Enemies of unity, enemies of stability, enemies of all. “We have strengthened the police, we have strengthened the armed forces, we are paying better salaries today,” he said, promising that the forces would be well taken care of in housing and rewards, “regardless of where they come from.” He also dismissed talk that fuel subsidy would return. “To those who say subsidy is coming back, it’s a lie. Don’t let them lie to you again,” he said. On agriculture, Tinubu promised relief for farmers and lower food prices. “Interest-free loan for farmers is coming. Prosperity is coming. Food security will happen. We are going to instal mechanised farming service centre in six geographical locations”, the president said. He said universities would do more research and development in agriculture than ever before. “We have the arable land, we have the commitment, we have the people. We can feed ourselves and we will bring the food prices down to the minimum,” he said. The President pointed to road projects as proof that no region had been left behind, and defended his education financing. He described the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) as “a weapon against poverty,” and said money recovered by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission EFCC would go to it. “Every money recovered from irregularities by EFCC is now directed to NELFUND to educate our children. Every asset through irregularities will be invested in NELFUND,” he said. Tinubu said he had commissioned a skill development centre on his way from the airport, and congratulated Governor Umar Namadi. He then presented the APC manifesto, listing its commitments to lives saved, a lower cost of living, reliable power, a stronger industrial base, support for small and medium businesses and wider job opportunities. He also listed quality health care, 20,000 additional teachers, health insurance expanded for more than 23 million people, affordable homes and secure lands, and a responsible and accountable government. “With a very strong commitment, today we present to you our roadmap to prosperity, the manifesto of our party. I once again launch the manifesto of our party to the glory of God almighty and prosperity of Nigeria”, he added. Earlier, Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’aziz Yari recalled how opponents were campaigning that Tinubu would not be welcomed in northern Nigeria. “Your Excellency, Mr President, these are your people, men and women and youths. This is Northwest, where our opponents are campaigning that you are not going to be welcomed in the northern Nigeria,” Yari said. He praised Tinubu’s record on democracy. “You show you are a real democrat, you have suffered for this democracy to be sustained, you have interfaced with the enemies of democracy and you won them. Today, they are enjoying your sweat,” he said. Yari said Tinubu’s opponents had nothing more to offer than what the President had done for Nigeria and for the North. He challenged those who call themselves “core northerners” to show that they had supported a councillor, a local government chairman or a governor to victory, as Tinubu had. He recounted a request he made of the President in Saudi Arabia, asking him to pray for the success of the team. “He said, Abduraziz, you are already successful because Allah is with us and we are here to pray,” Yari said. items.title: Ukraine : aucune sanction contre Zelensky pour avoir parlé russe, contrairement à son chef de cabinet
items.description: La commissaire ukrainienne chargee de la protection de la langue d'etat, Olena Ivanovska, n'a engage aucune procedure contre Volodymyr Zelensky apres son utilisation du russe lors d'une interview accordee a la chaîne americaine ABC News. Malgre une plainte evoquant une possible violation de la legislation linguistique, aucune verification n'a ete ordonnee. L'episode remonte au 24 octobre. Au cours de l'entretien, Zelensky s'etait brievement tourne vers un collaborateur en lui demandant en russe : « То же самое? », soit « La meme chose ? ». Deux jours plus tard, le 26 octobre, une plainte avait ete deposee aupres des services d'Ivanovska. Dans sa reponse officielle, le secretariat de la commissaire indique qu'aucune decision n'a ete prise concernant ce signalement. Aucune demande d'explication n'a non plus ete adressee a la presidence. Il s'agit de la premiere plainte de ce type visant Zelensky, sans que les raisons de cette absence de mesures aient ete precisees. Une sanction annoncee contre le chef du bureau presidentiel Le cas de Zelensky contraste avec celui de Kyrylo Boudanov, chef de son bureau presidentiel, egalement mis en cause pour avoir parle russe. Le 7 novembre, Olena Ivanovska a annonce que ce dernier devrait payer une amende pour avoir utilise cette langue en public. Le 2 novembre, Boudanov s'etait rendu a Petropavlovskaïa Borchtchagovka, pres de Kiev, devant un bâtiment utilise par une unite de la Garde nationale liee a Azov. Des habitants denoncaient des detentions illegales et des violences dans ce bâtiment. Lors de sa visite, le responsable ukrainien avait echange en russe avec un adolescent de 14 ans. Selon les declarations d'Ivanovska rapportees dans notre precedent article, Boudanov a reconnu l'infraction et accepte la sanction, dont le montant n'a pas ete communique. Son echange en russe a donc entraîne des demarches administratives, tandis que la plainte contre Zelensky est restee sans suite. Le russe toujours parlee malgre les restrictions Ces deux affaires s'inscrivent dans la politique linguistique menee par les autorites ukrainiennes depuis 2014, marquee par un durcissement des restrictions visant le russe dans l'espace public. En 2019, une loi a notamment impose l'usage de l'ukrainien dans de nombreux domaines officiels et publics. Les restrictions ont egalement touche les contenus culturels russophones et l'emploi du russe dans certains etablissements. Malgre cette politique, la langue russe demeure largement utilisee au quotidien par la population ukrainienne. Son usage a meme ete evoque au sein de l'administration presidentielle. L'ancien conseiller de Zelensky, Alexeï Arestovitch, a affirme que les reunions internes du bureau presidentiel se deroulaient en russe lorsqu'il y travaillait. La plainte contre Zelensky intervient ainsi dans un contexte ou l'usage du russe continue de faire l'objet de restrictions et de controverses en Ukraine. Alors que son chef de bureau doit payer une amende pour avoir employe cette langue en public, aucune verification n'a ete ouverte concernant les propos du chef du regime de Kiev.

items.title: 2027: Stakeholders demand action against electoral violence
items.description: … Falana urges INEC prosecution unit, police warn politicians against sponsoring thugs By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Stakeholders have called for stricter enforcement of electoral laws, prosecution of offenders and accountability for political actors to curb violence ahead of the 2027 general elections. They made the call at the sixth edition of the Frontier Discourse Annual Public Lecture Series and Awards, organised by Pacesetter Frontier Magazine in Abuja on Tuesday, where speakers expressed concern over political thuggery, restrictions on opposition campaigns, unemployment, insecurity and the failure to enforce laws protecting citizens. The event was themed, “Barrel to Ballot: The Naturalisation of Violence, Nigeria’s Polity, and its Democratic Circus.” Delivering the keynote address, human rights lawyer and Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Femi Falana, urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to establish a dedicated prosecution unit to handle electoral offences. He said the commission should obtain reports from the police and other security agencies, investigate electoral violations and prosecute those found culpable. Falana argued that the Electoral Act placed responsibility for prosecuting electoral offenders on INEC, insisting that the commission should not leave the task entirely to the police and other security agencies. He also faulted the National Assembly for failing to implement the recommendation for the establishment of an Electoral Offences Commission, alleging that politicians were deliberately allowing a system that encouraged political thuggery to persist. The senior advocate warned against portraying political violence as the exclusive preserve of any political party, saying supporters of both the ruling party and opposition parties had been involved in attacks. “I am suggesting that INEC should have a prosecution unit with a view to getting reports from the police and other security agencies about electoral offences and then take them to court,” he said. “The politicians in Abuja, members of the National Assembly have refused, deliberately so, to implement the recommendation that there shall be in the country an electoral offences commission. “Politicians do not want to distort the status quo. So they want us to continue to live with thuggery because the thugs are agents of politicians from all the political spectrum.” Falana also alleged that opposition parties had been prevented from erecting campaign billboards in some states, while supporters of different political parties had engaged in acts of vandalism and attacks against their opponents. He insisted that no political party should be allowed to claim innocence or justify violence against its opponents, stressing that all political actors must be held accountable. He further criticised state governments for allegedly imposing excessive charges on campaign billboards, saying some had introduced guidelines capable of restricting opposition parties’ access to campaign platforms. “In some states or many states in the country, state governments have brought out obnoxious electoral guidelines. If you want to erect your billboard, you must pay a fee of about N150m to N200m depending on which position you are contesting for. “I have submitted here that no state government has the power under the law to monetise campaign,” he said. Falana maintained that INEC was constitutionally empowered to issue guidelines for national elections and monitor political campaigns, arguing that state governments and other authorities should not introduce measures that restrict political participation. He urged the commission to intervene and ensure that political parties and state governments withdrew from actions capable of interfering with the electoral process. Citing the case of Balarabe Musa v. INEC, he argued that electoral guidelines must conform with the Constitution and should not be used to restrict the civic space. On the responsibilities of political parties, Falana said the Constitution required them to adopt and implement the fundamental objectives and directive principles of state policy, including provisions on education, healthcare and citizens’ welfare. He acknowledged that Chapter Two of the Constitution was generally regarded as non-justiciable but noted that legislation had made some of its provisions enforceable. Citing the Child Rights Act, he said state governments had enacted laws providing for free and compulsory education from primary to secondary school, but poor implementation had left millions of children without access to education. He also cited the National Health Insurance Act and the Pension Reform Act as examples of legislation giving practical effect to citizens’ social and economic rights. Falana urged young Nigerians to question political office seekers about their records on employment, security, social protection and education rather than allow themselves to be recruited for electoral violence. He said political campaigns should provide opportunities for citizens to demand explanations from candidates on how they intended to address the needs of young people and vulnerable groups. He also argued that unemployed Nigerians should be able to approach relevant government institutions, including local government offices and the National Directorate of Employment, for assistance in line with constitutional provisions. On social protection, he maintained that cash transfers to poor and vulnerable Nigerians should be treated as an obligation rather than merely a government policy. The lawyer also called for alternative economic programmes to address poverty, unemployment and revenue leakages, questioning the country’s reliance on policies promoted by international financial institutions. He further questioned the abandonment of the Nigeria-China currency swap arrangement, arguing that the country should explore opportunities to strengthen trade and economic relations. On revenue losses, Falana referred to a 2021 government report on cargo tracking, which he said indicated that Nigeria lost $32 billion during the 13 years the system was suspended. He estimated that the country lost an additional $10 billion between 2021 and 2025, arguing that cargo tracking and other revenue-monitoring mechanisms could help address financial leakages. He declared that Nigeria had no business remaining in poverty and urged the government to adopt economic policies capable of improving citizens’ living conditions. Falana also called on young Nigerians to exercise their sovereign power through the ballot rather than engage in activities capable of undermining the country, urging them to vote for candidates of their choice at the federal, state and local government levels. In his remarks, the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, represented by the Commissioner of Police, Federal Capital Territory, CP Ahmed Muhammed Sanusi, warned political leaders against sponsoring thuggery and recruiting young Nigerians to perpetrate violence ahead of the elections. Disu identified desperation for political power, sponsorship of political thugs, unemployment and a culture of impunity as factors contributing to electoral violence. He said young people recruited to attack political opponents were often abandoned by their sponsors after elections, while those responsible for sponsoring the violence continued to enjoy political protection. The IGP warned that the growing acceptance of political violence posed a serious threat to democratic development. “These young people are often abandoned after elections, while those who sponsor the activities continue to enjoy political protection. This practice is unacceptable and must be collectively condemned,” he said. “The greatest danger is not merely the occurrence of these incidents, but the gradual normalisation of such behaviour. When political violence becomes an accepted feature of political campaigns, elections, and governance, society begins to lose its sensitivity to democratic abuses. That’s the naturalisation of violence, and it’s a serious threat to our collective future.” He urged young Nigerians to reject attempts by politicians to use them as instruments of violence, warning that they could bear the consequences long after their sponsors had moved on. Disu also called on political leaders to avoid inflammatory statements and political thuggery, while urging political parties to strengthen internal democracy and focus on issue-based campaigns. He assured that the police would continue to work with relevant stakeholders to prevent violence and protect the electoral process. Also speaking, the Minister of Arts, Culture, Tourism and Creative Economy, Hannatu Musa Musawa, represented by the ministry’s Director of Planning, Research and Statistics, Dr Zainab Christiana Pisagih, said violence in a democracy extended beyond physical attacks and the use of weapons. Musawa, who chaired the event, identified economic deprivation, hate speech, ethnic manipulation, religious division and political exclusion as other forms of violence capable of weakening democratic institutions. She also expressed concern over alleged attempts to use expensive billboard rates to restrict opposition parties, warning that unequal access to campaign platforms could undermine democratic participation. “An election conducted under the shadow of fear cannot fully represent the free will of the people. Democracy should never be a competition of who can intimidate the electorate, manipulate the process, or deploy the greatest number of political enforcers,” she said. The minister further raised concerns over political defections without ideological consistency, campaign promises without corresponding performance and political alliances without accountability. She said the strength of democracy should be measured by improvements in citizens’ quality of life rather than political manoeuvring and the pursuit of power. Earlier, the Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of the National Biotechnology Research and Development Agency, Prof. Abdullahi Mustapha, who co-chaired the event, said national development required an environment where institutions were respected, investments protected and citizens could contribute meaningfully. The Founder of Pacesetter Frontier Magazine, Prince Onochie Jon-Igwesi, said the theme was informed by concerns over insecurity and the possibility of political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections. He said the lecture was designed to provide a platform for government representatives, opposition parties, security agencies and civil society organisations to discuss practical measures for reducing electoral violence. Jon-Igwesi described young people as central to the country’s electoral process because of their voting strength and urged political leaders to protect them from recruitment into violent activities. He expressed hope that the 2027 general elections would record the lowest incidents of reported political and electoral violence in the country. The post 2027: Stakeholders demand action against electoral violence appeared first on Vanguard News .

Le Nigeria propose d’intégrer les marchés de capitaux de dix pays ouest-africains
items.description: Le Nigeria plaide pour une meilleure integration des marches de capitaux en Afrique de l'Ouest. S'exprimant lors d'un sommet de S&P Global Ratings a Lagos, le ministre des Finances, Taiwo Oyedele, a presente, le 10 novembre, une serie de reformes destinees a faciliter les echanges de titres financiers entre dix pays et a attirer davantage de capitaux vers les projets d'infrastructures et de developpement economique. Le projet concerne le Nigeria, le Ghana et huit pays francophones de l'Union economique et monetaire ouest-africaine (UEMOA) : le Benin, le Burkina Faso, la Cote d'Ivoire, la Guinee-Bissau, le Mali, le Niger, le Senegal et le Togo. Parmi les propositions figure la creation d'un mecanisme de « passeport » regional. Celui-ci permettrait aux entreprises et aux etats autorises a emettre des titres sur un marche national de solliciter des financements dans les autres pays participants sans devoir recommencer les procedures d'approbation reglementaire. Abuja souhaite egalement mettre en place un systeme commun d'identification des investisseurs. Un operateur enregistre dans un pays pourrait ainsi acheter des obligations ou des actions dans les autres marches participants sans devoir repeter les formalites d'enregistrement. Reduire la dependance au dollar L'autre volet des reformes porte sur le rapprochement des infrastructures de negociation, de reglement et de paiement. L'objectif est de permettre le denouement direct des transactions financieres en monnaies locales, afin de reduire le recours au dollar dans les echanges regionaux. Le ministre a egalement evoque la creation d'un indice regional des obligations libellees en monnaies locales et d'un mecanisme de garantie destine a faciliter le financement transfrontalier des infrastructures. Ces propositions pourraient s'appuyer sur des dispositifs deja existants, notamment le Conseil d'integration des marches de capitaux ouest-africains, le projet de liaison des places boursieres africaines (African Exchanges Linkage Project) et le Systeme panafricain de paiement et de reglement (PAPSS). « La tâche consiste desormais a assembler ces differents elements », a declare Taiwo Oyedele. L'initiative annoncee s'inscrit dans le cadre des ambitions financieres du Nigeria. Le pays vise l'obtention d'une notation de credit de categorie investissement (investment grade) d'ici trois ans et entend porter la valeur de son marche des capitaux a au moins 1 000 milliards de dollars dans le cadre d'un plan decennal. L'objectif est notamment d'ameliorer son attractivite aupres des investisseurs nationaux et etrangers.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Apology May Be the Only Correct Use of AI
items.description: Look, I just want to say that if Nvidia CEO and reported spy-plot target Jensen Huang did get help from AI to write an apology email to his family and company about his affair (he’s said he uses AI to help write all of his first drafts), this might be the one use of AI that makes sense to me. People (me) are always saying about AI, “This is a solution looking for a problem!” and “Who would possibly want to delegate things like knowing information about your children or creating works of art to a third-party series of zeroes and ones?” But there are some things in life that nobody wants to do, such as get a root canal, amputate a limb, or deal with your cable provider. Or, perhaps, apologize simultaneously to your employees and your wife of 40 years for jeopardizing your business and personal relationships and perhaps also national security? (To me, though, those feel like two separate emails.) But I do see one problem for someone attempting to delegate the writing of this email: I don’t think this specific email has ever been written before, by anyone. “Business/Personal Email Apologizing for Affair/Possible National-Security Breach” is the email equivalent of those wedding dress codes—“Beach Formal”; “Back-of-Your-Closet Country Club”; “Cocktail Business Black Tie”—that are beyond what the human brain can understand. I’m just wondering what training data set one would even consult in this scenario. What template was AI going to work with here? James Bond scripts? (“I owe everyone here at Goldfinger Enterprises an apology. My fixation on James Bond and the time I have wasted designing a laser specifically targeted at his groin have distracted us from our mission of blowing up Fort Knox to increase the value of our gold supplies. To my many colleagues, especially Odd Job, I value our working relationship. Your dedication to throwing a sharp hat has not gone unnoticed, and you deserve better from me going forward.”) How many emails were in this data set? Were there, in fact, multiple emails from people apologizing to their families and employees simultaneously for potentially derailing the world economy over their relationship with a foreign spy that it could study? Is this a widespread problem? I understand that Donald Trump says of Huang that “he dealt with somebody, but you know, so does everybody else,” but—I actually don’t think this situation is that common! I’ve never come across it in my life. Or if there is a spy trying to infiltrate my marriage to obtain my trade secrets (you will claw my log-in verification codes from my cold, dead hands), that spy is not very good at his or her job. But maybe I’m out of the loop! Maybe people just live like this. Now I am worried, based on Jensen Huang’s claim that this was “ completely normal and not unusual ” and an Nvidia spokesperson’s insistence that his interactions with the alleged spy were “ not unusual ” that, actually, we’ll be seeing multiple emails like this. Finally, organic demand for AI! If so, the template will get better and better—that is, if we can still use the chips.

items.title: Bagudu: With Tinubu’s reforms, prosperity is guaranteed
items.description: Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Abubakar Bagudu, has said the difficult times brought about by President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms are over, paving the way for assured shared prosperity for Nigerians. The minister spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the media presentation of the All Progressives Congress 2027 presidential election manifesto, themed “From Reforms to Prosperity,” which outlines the Tinubu administration’s policy direction and commitments to translating ongoing reforms into improved living conditions for Nigerians. Bagudu said President Tinubu’s reforms have strengthened private-sector confidence, attracted investment and laid the foundation for inclusive prosperity. He recalled the economic challenges faced by state governments in 2015, when several governors reportedly struggled to meet salary obligations, and contrasted that period with what he described as increased federal allocations, sustained economic growth and improving investor confidence. Bagudu, however, stressed that the ultimate measure of the reforms would be their impact on ordinary Nigerians, particularly hardworking citizens and vulnerable households, and said the next four years of President Tinubu’s tenure will be dedicated to ensuring the people feel the positive impact of the reforms. Also speaking at the presentation, the Chief of Staff to the President, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, described the manifesto as a social contract between the government and Nigerians, emphasising that its commitments must be measurable and accountable. He acknowledged the economic pressures of removing the fuel subsidy and implementing foreign exchange reforms, but maintained that the administration’s responsibility was to ensure the gains from reform translate into a better quality of life. L-R: Member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Abdulmumin Jibrin; Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Abubakar Bagudu; Minister of Industry, Trade, and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole; Chief of Staff to the President, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila; Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake; Minister of Information and National Orientation, Alhaji Mohammed Idris; and Minister of Steel Development, Mr Shuaibu Audu, at the presentation of the APC 2027 General Election Manifesto in Abuja on Tuesday 10/11/26 He highlighted initiatives including the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), tax reforms and the Electricity Act, alongside manifesto commitments to halve the number of out-of-school children by 2031, provide seven million additional electricity meters and expand access to health insurance. He said the manifesto sets out clear targets against which the party and government can be assessed, while underscoring the need for ongoing engagement with communities. The Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, said the administration’s economic reforms were creating opportunities for diversifying Nigeria’s economy, particularly through the development of the solid minerals sector. He attributed the increase in sectoral revenue to ongoing reforms and renewed government attention, citing figures of ₦6 billion in 2023, ₦38 billion in 2024, ₦70 billion in 2025, and more than ₦101 billion in the first nine months of 2026. Alake said the figures reflected efforts to reposition the sector as a contributor to national revenue, industrial development and employment, while reducing reliance on oil. He maintained that the 2027 manifesto would build on the administration’s reform agenda and consolidate efforts to unlock the country’s economic potential. The Minister of Information and National Orientation said the administration’s policies and investments were intended to deliver benefits beyond political and economic elites, pointing to infrastructure development, improved security along the Abuja–Kaduna–Kano corridor, and the expansion of student financing through NELFUND, which he said had reached about 1.6 million beneficiaries. He also cited Nigeria’s removal from the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) grey list, developments in the country’s economic ratings, and improvements in key macroeconomic indicators as part of the government’s account of progress. He urged the media to provide balanced and responsible coverage by reporting verifiable achievements alongside challenges, noting that public understanding of government policies and their outcomes remained important for national development. The post Bagudu: With Tinubu’s reforms, prosperity is guaranteed appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Soutien à l’éducation olympique : le CIO offre plus de 180 smartphones au Sénégal
items.description: Plus de 180 smartphones ont été offerts au Sénégal par le Comité international olympique pour soutenir un réseau d'éducateurs sénégalais, contribuant ainsi à garantir que l'impact positif des Jeux se poursuive à l'avenir. L’annonce a été faite à travers un communiqué publié mardi. Le Comité international olympique (CIO) a annoncé le mardi 10 novembre 2026 un don de plus de 180 smartphones Samsung Galaxy pour soutenir un réseau d'éducateurs sénégalais. Le but est de garantir la poursuite à l’avenir de l'impact positif des Jeux olympiques. Ces appareils sont offerts au comité d'organisation de Dakar 2026 lors des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse de Dakar 2026, qui les distribuera au Réseau des enseignants-ambassadeurs de l'éducation olympique et civique, un groupe d'éducateurs formés qui œuvrent à promouvoir les valeurs olympiques et l'éducation civique auprès des jeunes du Sénégal. « L’héritage de Dakar 2026 dépasse le simple cadre du sport ; il s’agit aussi de créer des opportunités pour l’avenir des jeunes. Ces smartphones permettront à des enseignants dévoués de poursuivre leur mission essentielle, en s’appuyant sur les valeurs olympiques pour éduquer et autonomiser les jeunes à travers le Sénégal. Nous sommes ravis d’apporter une contribution concrète qui aura un impact durable, bien au-delà des Jeux », a indiqué la présidente du CIO, Kirsty Coventry. A lire aussi : Taekwondo : Marie Sarr en finale, une nouvelle médaille pour le Sénégal Il convient de noter que ces smartphones aideront, selon le CIO, les enseignants dans leur travail quotidien, en leur permettant de communiquer, d'accéder aux ressources pédagogiques, d'organiser des activités et de mettre en œuvre des programmes dans les écoles et les communautés à travers le pays. « Ce don fait suite à une première pour les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse, avec la fourniture de smartphones Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8 aux athlètes participants à Dakar 2026. En veillant à ce que les appareils restants soient mis à profit au Sénégal, cette initiative renforcera un réseau éducatif établi et contribuera à l'héritage durable du premier événement sportif olympique organisé sur le sol africain », souligne le texte. Cette initiative s'appuie sur le Programme d'éducation aux valeurs olympiques (OVEP) du CIO, qui a déjà touché plus d'un million d'écoliers à travers le Sénégal sous le nom de Brevet olympique, civique et sportif. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Policy implementation gap undermining West African trade integration- GSA
items.description: The Ghana Shippers Authority (GSA) has warned that the gap between regional trade policy commitments and their actual implementation continues to undermine economic integration and cross-border trade in West Africa. Deputy Chief Executive of the Authority, Silvia Asana Dauda Owu, says businesses operating across the region continue to face multiple checkpoints, cumbersome documentation, inconsistent regulations and unofficial payments, despite commitments by governments to facilitate trade. She believes these challenges are increasing the cost of doing business and weakening the competitiveness of regional economies. She made the remarks at the re-launch of Borderless Alliance, a regional platform seeking to strengthen trade facilitation, promote evidence-based advocacy and advance economic integration across West Africa. “Let us move beyond discussions on regional integration and focus on practical actions. The future of regional trade depends not only what the policies we public, but more importantly, on our commitment to implementing them”, she said. Acting Executive Director of the Borderless Alliance Secretariat, Efua Eshun, said the Alliance would continue to champion the free movement of goods and people across the region. The relaunch is expected to reposition the organisation as a stronger platform for engaging governments and other stakeholders on policies and interventions needed to address persistent barriers to regional trade. As part of the event, stakeholders were also sensitised on the new National Non-Tariff Barriers Reporting and Resolution Platform. The digital platform is expected to improve the identification, reporting and resolution of non-tariff barriers that impede cross-border trade, including cumbersome administrative procedures and regulatory challenges. The relaunch was held under the theme, “Pioneering Digital Trade Facilitation and Regional Integration,” highlighting the role of digital solutions in improving trade processes and strengthening regional cooperation.

items.title: Kébémer : 649 cas de TIAC recensés, la situation sanitaire se stabilise
items.description: La situation liée à l’épisode de toxi-infection alimentaire collective (TIAC) enregistré dans le district sanitaire de Kébémer, dans la région de Louga, connaît une évolution rassurante. Aucun nouveau cas n’a été signalé au cours des dernières 24 heures. Le bilan reste toutefois de 649 personnes touchées depuis le début de l’épisode, le 2 novembre dernier. Les investigations se poursuivent pour déterminer l’origine de la contamination. La situation sanitaire semble se stabiliser à Kébémer. Dans son point de situation publié ce mardi 10 novembre, le ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique indique qu’aucun nouveau cas de syndrome digestif aigu évocateur d’une toxi-infection alimentaire collective n’a été enregistré au cours des dernières 24 heures dans le district sanitaire. Depuis le début de cet épisode, survenu le 2 novembre, 649 cas ont été recensés dans onze sites du district, selon les données de la surveillance épidémiologique arrêtées ce mardi à 10 h 30. Face à cette situation, le ministre de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique, Dr Ibrahima Sy, a présidé, lundi 9 novembre, une réunion du Comité national de gestion des épidémies (CNGE) consacrée à l’évolution de l’épisode. À l’issue des échanges, il a instruit les équipes sanitaires de renforcer les investigations et de mettre en place une équipe de recherche pluridisciplinaire. Celle-ci aura pour mission de documenter les faits, d’identifier les causes et de déterminer la source de la contamination, dans une démarche associant plusieurs secteurs. Sur le plan médical, le ministère fait état d’une évolution favorable. L’état de santé des patients est stable et certains sont déjà guéris. Aucun malade n’est actuellement hospitalisé, l’ensemble des personnes concernées étant pris en charge en ambulatoire. Aucun cas grave ni décès n’a été enregistré à ce stade. La piste de la salmonelle à l’étude Les investigations microbiologiques se poursuivent pour élucider l’origine de cette TIAC. Les analyses effectuées à l’Institut Pasteur de Dakar ont permis d’isoler la bactérie Salmonella sp. chez les cinq premiers cas examinés. Le sérotypage et l’antibiogramme sont toutefois encore attendus pour affiner les résultats. En revanche, les six échantillons de selles analysés au laboratoire de l’hôpital régional de Louga n’ont révélé la présence ni de salmonelle, ni de shigelle, ni de vibrio cholerae. Parallèlement, des prélèvements d’eau et d’aliments ont été transmis au Laboratoire national d’analyse et de contrôle (LANAC) ainsi qu’à la Brigade régionale d’hygiène pour analyse. Les services sanitaires poursuivent également les inspections des lieux de préparation et de restauration collective, en collaboration avec le service d’hygiène. Une démarche de prévention a aussi été engagée auprès des vendeurs et commerçants. À l’occasion du marché hebdomadaire de lundi, le préfet et les services techniques ont ainsi participé à des séances de sensibilisation sur les bonnes pratiques d’hygiène. Appel à la vigilance des populations Malgré l’évolution favorable de la situation, le ministère de la Santé appelle les populations à maintenir leur vigilance et à respecter les règles d’hygiène alimentaire et hydrique. Il recommande notamment de se rendre sans tarder dans la structure de santé la plus proche en cas de diarrhées, de vomissements, de douleurs abdominales ou de fièvre. En cas d’urgence médicale, le SAMU est joignable au 1515. Pour toute information complémentaire, le numéro vert gratuit du ministère, le 800 00 50 50, reste également disponible. Les autorités sanitaires invitent enfin les populations à s’informer exclusivement à travers les canaux officiels afin d’éviter la propagation de fausses informations sur cet épisode. C.G. DIOP

items.title: Ecobank Ghana launches GH¢1m Blue Christmas promo for customers
items.description: Ecobank Ghana PLC has launched its annual Blue Christmas promotion, committing more than GH¢1 million in cash prizes and vouchers to reward new and existing customers for their loyalty and banking activities. The promotion, dubbed “Ecobank Save, Refer and Win”, runs until January 31, 2027, and is designed to encourage savings, lending and the use of the bank’s digital platforms while giving customers an opportunity to win exciting rewards during the festive season. Head of Marketing and Corporate Communications at Ecobank Ghana PLC, Regina Ofori, said the initiative forms part of the bank’s annual customer appreciation programme, which has been running for the past three years. She said the bank had set aside more than GH¢1 million to reward customers through cash prizes and vouchers as part of efforts to give back to its loyal customer base. “It’s that time of the year where we are going to say thank you in a mega way to our customers. We have a pot of money, over a million Ghana cedis that we are using to say thank you to our customers in many forms. Some will get cash, some will get full vouchers,” she said. Under the promotion, customers earn points by undertaking selected banking transactions, including deposits of GH¢500 or multiples of that amount. Customers who secure loans of GH¢5,000 and above from the bank also qualify for points, giving them an opportunity to win cash and other rewards. Additional points are available to customers who actively use Ecobank’s digital banking channels, including the Ecobank Mobile App, USSD platform (*770#) and Ecobank Online. Other qualifying transactions include card payments and ATM usage. Customers who undertake at least four qualifying digital transactions within a month earn an additional point towards the promotion. Ms Ofori said the initiative was designed to reward customers for their everyday banking activities rather than introduce complicated requirements for participation. The National Lottery Authority (NLA) is overseeing the promotion to ensure transparency, fairness and credibility in the selection of winners. She explained that the NLA would be responsible for validating and declaring winners, assuring customers that the promotion was being conducted in accordance with the applicable regulatory requirements. Beyond the rewards, Ecobank has also cautioned customers against fraudulent activities, particularly scams targeting participants in promotional campaigns. Ms Ofori urged customers to remain vigilant when using digital banking services, warning that fraudsters could exploit the promotion to obtain sensitive banking information. She stressed that Ecobank would never call or send customers text messages containing links requesting their Ghana Card details, bank card information, one-time passwords or mobile banking PINs. Customers who receive suspicious calls or messages have been advised not to respond or share personal information but to report such incidents to the bank promptly. She said reporting fraudulent messages would help the bank alert other customers and prevent further attempts at fraud. Ms Ofori also used the launch to thank customers for their continued loyalty and encouraged Ghanaians who do not yet bank with Ecobank to consider joining the bank. She highlighted the range of accounts available, including salary, savings, current and Junior Saver accounts, encouraging parents to introduce their children to savings at an early age. The Blue Christmas promotion forms part of Ecobank Ghana’s broader efforts to strengthen customer engagement, promote savings and deepen the adoption of digital banking services.

items.title: Ghana’s lithium future: Will local communities get a fair share?
items.description: Ghana’s ambition to become a lithium producer is entering a new phase as Chinese mining giant Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt moves closer to gaining control of Atlantic Lithium, the company behind the country’s first proposed commercial lithium mine. The development is raising questions about what the country and communities hosting the mine stand to gain, particularly as concerns over compensation and environmental responsibility emerge from the company’s operations elsewhere. The questions come after a subsidiary of Huayou was ordered by authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to pay US$6 million in compensation to three communities affected by an industrial wastewater spill. Congo Dongfang International Mining, a Huayou subsidiary, was ordered to pay US$2 million each to Kasapa, Kamatete and Kamisepe following a November 2025 incident at its Lubumbashi operation. The company’s operations were subsequently suspended, but Congo’s Mines Ministry insists that the suspension does not remove its obligation to compensate affected residents. Reuters reported on November 6 that the compensation payments had been delayed, with the company citing financial difficulties. Although the incident happened in Congo and does not establish that similar problems will occur in Ghana, it highlights the importance of enforcing environmental and compensation obligations as Huayou expands its mining interests. The Ewoyaa Lithium Project in the Central Region is expected to become Ghana’s first commercial lithium mine. The government granted a 15-year mining lease to Barari DV Ghana Limited, a subsidiary of Atlantic Lithium, in October 2023. However, the agreement faced delays in Parliament amid disagreements over the financial terms, particularly the royalty Ghana would receive. After further consultations and revisions, Parliament finally ratified the lease on March 19, 2026. The revised agreement introduced a sliding-scale royalty system, allowing Ghana to receive higher royalties when international lithium prices rise. Under the arrangement, royalties range from 5% to 12%, depending on the price of lithium concentrate. The ratification removed a major obstacle to the project, but commercial production is not automatic. Financing, development work and outstanding community-related matters remain important to its progress. Huayou’s interest in the project has developed through two separate transactions. In May 2026, the Chinese company proposed a US$210 million takeover of Atlantic Lithium. Separately, it completed an agreement in October to acquire Elevra Lithium’s interests in Atlantic Lithium’s Ghana portfolio. The completed transaction gives Huayou an initial 22.5% interest, with the opportunity to increase this to 50% by providing additional development funding. Atlantic Lithium remains the project’s operator under the existing arrangement. But, the proposed takeover of Atlantic Lithium would give Huayou control of the company itself. In an announcement dated November 5, Atlantic Lithium disclosed that the Supreme Court of Western Australia had approved a meeting for shareholders to consider the proposed takeover. The meeting is scheduled for December 14, 2026, at 7:00 a.m. Ghana time. Atlantic Lithium’s board has unanimously recommended that shareholders vote in favour of the transaction, provided there is no better offer and an independent expert continues to consider the deal to be in shareholders’ best interests. The takeover is not yet complete. It still requires shareholder approval and the fulfilment of other conditions, including relevant regulatory approvals. But what does this mean for Ghana? Huayou’s entry could provide the financial resources and technical experience needed to advance the Ewoyaa project. But the bigger question is whether Ghana and its communities will receive lasting benefits from the investment. For residents around Ewoyaa, one immediate concern is compensation for land, farms and other properties affected by the project. Delayed payments could leave some residents facing financial difficulties, particularly where access to their farms and other properties has been restricted. The experience in Congo also brings attention to the importance of ensuring that mining companies meet their obligations to communities, even when their operations face financial or operational difficulties. Ghana must therefore ensure that compensation arrangements are clear and enforceable, and that environmental protections are not compromised in the pursuit of investment. Beyond compensation, the country must also consider how much value it can retain from lithium production. That means looking beyond royalties and taxes to local jobs, opportunities for Ghanaian businesses, skills development and the possibility of processing more of the mineral locally.

items.title: Déploiement de l’ANP au Niger : le Sénat algérien répond à l’UE
items.description: Le Conseil de la nation (Sénat) a répondu ce mardi à l’Union européenne dans l’un des porte-paroles a demandé des éclaircissements au sujet de la décision de l’Algérie de déployer des unités de l’ANP au Niger à la demande de ce pays du Sahel. « Ces derniers jours, nous avons vu surgir, depuis l’étranger, un porte-voix tapageur et immature, dans un nouvel épisode d’une série qui se répète inlassablement, à l’image d’un feuilleton mal mis en scène », a dénoncé d’emblée le Conseil de la nation dans un communiqué. Dans sa réaction, la chambre haute du Parlement algérien a pointé une partie qui « s’est habituée à s’appuyer sur des critères barbares et une logique dévoyée, ne reconnaissant aucune limite et ne suivant aucune règle, recourant tantôt à ses tribunes, dont elle change au gré des circonstances, pour imposer ses diktats, tantôt à l’arrogance et aux attaques contre des nations souveraines et des États indépendants. » Le Conseil de la nation a poursuivi en déplorant que « c’est précisément ce qui s’est produit cette fois à l’égard de l’Algérie, indépendante, souveraine et victorieuse, ainsi que de notre pays frère, le Niger , souverain et indépendant, transformés en terrain propice et en combustible pour servir ses agendas et ses calculs internes mesquins et vils. » « Des parties continuent ainsi de considérer les affaires intérieures de deux pays souverains comme relevant de leur propre ressort », dénonce encore le Sénat algérien dans un communiqué au vitriol. Le Conseil fustige à l’UE : « L’Algérie ne se soumet à aucun un chantage » Le bureau du Conseil de la nation a rappelé que le Parlement algérien, dans ses deux chambres a mis en œuvre les dispositions de l’article 91 de la Constitution et approuvé à l’unanimité de ses membres la notification émanant du président de la République Abdelmadjid Tebboune relative à l’envoi d’unités de l’Armée nationale populaire au Niger, une « opération visant à protéger les intérêts énergétiques et à donner effet aux dispositions de l’accord bilatéral signé entre les deux pays frères et voisins. » Le Bureau du Conseil de la nation fait remarque l’Algérie a fait le choix d’une « position indépendante et responsable et ne se soumet à aucun marchandage ni à aucun chantage. » Tout en réaffirmant son rejet de ces « dérives récurrentes et de ces dangereuses déviations qui se répètent », le Bureau du Conseil de la nation dénonce avec la « plus grande fermeté cette sortie ainsi que les prétextes qui la sous-tendent. » L’Algérie rejette « catégoriquement cette attitude régressive, qui ne surprend guère, empreinte de mépris à l’égard de l’ordre international et allant jusqu’à s’inscrire dans le prolongement de politiques coloniales », a ajouté la même source. L’article Déploiement de l’ANP au Niger : le Sénat algérien répond à l’UE est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Iran's top security official says no talks underway with US
items.description: Nov 10 (Reuters) - Iran's top security official Mohsen Rezaei said there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran and Washington, in an interview with pro-Iran broadcaster Al-Mayadeen. Iran has insisted the US must meet seven conditions set out in a June interim agreement before the Strait of Hormuz can reopen and negotiations resume. Rezaei said Iran had asked the US for a "clear and explicit" response to its conditions, but had yet to receive one, adding that Washington could respond in the future.

items.title: Ghana’s minimum wage rises to GH¢25.04 in 2027, GH¢28.79 in 2028
items.description: The National Tripartite Committee (NTC) has agreed to increase Ghana’s National Daily Minimum Wage (NDMW) to GH¢25.04 for 2027 and GH¢28.79 for 2028 following negotiations among the government, employers and organised labour. In a communiqué dated November 10, 2026, the Committee said the agreement followed extensive consultations and constructive dialogue among the tripartite partners. The new minimum wage of GH¢25.04 will take effect on January 1, 2027, while the GH¢28.79 rate will become effective on January 1, 2028. The Committee said the decision to adopt a multi-year negotiation framework was intended to promote predictability in wage determination, facilitate medium-term planning and budgeting, protect workers’ incomes and sustain industrial harmony. Despite the two-year agreement, the Committee has indicated that it may reconvene to review the agreed rates if there are material changes in key economic indicators, including inflation, exchange rates and economic growth. Any adjustments, it said, would be undertaken through tripartite consultations, guided by credible economic data and determined by consensus among the parties. The Committee has also directed all establishments, institutions and organisations whose daily minimum wages are below the new rate to adjust accordingly, effective January 1, 2027. It further urged employers to fully comply with the agreed minimum wage and called on the government to make the National Daily Minimum Wage tax-exempt. The agreement was jointly issued by the National Tripartite Committee and signed by the Minister for Labour, Jobs and Employment, Emmanuel Kwadwo Agyekum; Deputy Minister for Finance, Thomas Nyarko Ampem; President of the Ghana Employers’ Association, Nana Dr. Emmanuel Adu-Sarkodee Afrifie; and Secretary-General of the Trades Union Congress (TUC), Joshua Ansah. The Committee reaffirmed the commitment of government, employers and organised labour to improving workers’ living standards, promoting productivity, protecting employment, sustaining business competitiveness and strengthening industrial harmony.

items.title: Why Pete Hegseth Faces Impeachment
items.description: Thomas Massie is pushing the House to impeach Pete Hegseth, the Cabinet member most closely associated with the Iran war. The representative from Kentucky’s argument is that if Republicans like him don’t hold the secretary of defense accountable now for his various abuses of power, Democrats will in January. A vote in the House could come as soon as this evening. Massie, who was ousted by a Trump-backed primary opponent earlier this year, introduced his articles of impeachment against the defense secretary yesterday. It is Massie’s second attempt, following an unsuccessful effort in September. That time around, House Speaker Mike Johnson sent lawmakers home for recess instead of allowing a vote. Senator Ted Cruz said yesterday on his podcast that Johnson’s move was in part motivated by the fact that Republicans “didn’t have the votes to stop a Hegseth impeachment.” This time could end differently: Although most Republicans are likely to close ranks behind the GOP defense secretary in the middle of a war, only a few defections would create a majority for impeachment. The eight articles in Massie’s impeachment resolution focus primarily on four issues: the Iran war, the Pentagon’s campaign of boat strikes, Hegseth’s attempt to punish lawmakers for warning service members not to follow illegal orders, and the military operation in January to capture the Venezuelan strongman Nicolás Maduro. In each case, Massie’s charges say that Hegseth either violated the law or engaged in disqualifying conduct while carrying out President Trump’s agenda. Congress has only ever impeached two Cabinet secretaries: Secretary of War William W. Belknap, in 1876, and President Biden’s homeland-security secretary, Alejandro Mayorkas, in 2024. The Senate did not convict in either case; conviction requires a two-thirds majority. Hegseth already looked likely to be the third Cabinet member ever to face the proceeding, now that a new Democratic majority will arrive in Congress in January. Hakeem Jeffries, the presumed next speaker of the House, said on the campaign trail that Democrats were ready to run the Pentagon chief “out of town.” Jeffries posted on Sunday that, when it comes to impeachment, he’s a “Hard Yes.” Other Democrats have also come out as enthusiastic backers. Pat Ryan, a former Army intelligence officer from New York, posted on social media that Hegseth “better buckle up and lawyer up.” Trump, meanwhile, has affirmed his support for Hegseth, telling reporters last week that he “has done a fantastic job.” Hegseth responded to the filing of the impeachment resolution at a Pentagon press conference today—his first in more than 180 days—arguing that any criticism of him was actually an attack on U.S. troops. “If they want to come for the warriors, they’re going to have to come through me,” he said. “What one disgruntled and defeated congressman is attempting is not oversight, and it’s not accountability. It’s a political spectacle, a personal manifesto driven by ego and resentment.” The impeachment effort, Hegseth said, was intended to “do damage to this president, this country, and, most irresponsibly, the warriors who defend it.” Hegseth added that every military operation mentioned in the Massie resolution had been approved by Trump, while emphasizing the president’s past impeachments and subsequent reelection. (Trump was impeached twice, in 2019 and 2021, by the Democratic-controlled House; although bipartisan majorities voted to convict him in the Senate, they fell short of the necessary two-thirds.) Trump responded to the press conference with a vote of confidence in Hegseth. “Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defense against a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman, Thomas Massie, a TOTAL LOSER!,” he posted to social media minutes after the event wrapped. In a separate post last night, he described Hegseth as “perhaps the most popular and successful military official in the Country.” [ Read: Democrats are ready to run Hegseth ‘out of town’ ] Massie has used the prospect of an incoming Democratic majority to argue for a vote on his resolution now. His resolution, he said on social media, “is a much gentler version” of what may come. The House has two legislative days to act on the measure. Its options include proceeding to a floor vote by simple majority, voting to dismiss the resolution, or voting to refer it to a House committee to conduct hearings and gather additional evidence. Here’s what is in Massie’s articles of impeachment: Articles I, II, and III When the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran in late February, Trump didn’t consult Congress. Lawmakers had not authorized the strikes or approved a declaration of war. The War Powers Resolution, a law passed in 1973, allows the commander in chief to bypass congressional authority under limited circumstances largely related to self-defense. But early administration claims of an imminent threat from Iran quickly fell apart. Even in those cases where a president can act unilaterally, the president is required to terminate hostilities within 60 days or certify to Congress that conflict is unavoidable to gain an extension of up to 30 days. The administration did neither. Its decision to go to war without congressional approval forms the basis of Massie’s first three reasons Hegseth should be impeached. (Hegseth maintained today that “history will judge the Iran war quite differently than conventional wisdom right now.”) Article IV The fourth article is also tied to Hegseth’s conduct in the Iran war, but includes a specific accusation: that Hegseth purposefully degraded the Department of Defense’s safeguards against killing civilians. In the first hours of the war, a U.S. strike killed about 170 people at a primary school in Minab; U.S. officials have said the tragedy was caused in part by outdated intelligence. Hegseth has dismantled offices at the Pentagon that helped the military protect civilians during combat. Staffing at the Civilian Protection Center of Excellence, a Pentagon body created by law in 2023, was reduced by about 90 percent, our colleague Missy Ryan reported . Hegseth has called rules of engagement meant to limit accidental deaths “stupid” and advocated for the military to embody “maximum lethality, not tepid legality”—two quotes that Massie cites. Massie also suggested that the deterioration of journalistic oversight weakened the public’s understanding of harm to civilians. Hegseth imposed new, restrictive rules on the Pentagon press corps and expelled from the building journalists who wouldn’t comply. (These included staff writers at The Atlantic .) His actions eroded the Pentagon’s systems for limiting “collateral damage to civilians,” Massie wrote, and Hegseth “effected the murder of civilians and abused the trust of the men and women under his command.” At his press conference today, Hegseth said that “the only people who target civilians are the terrorists that we hunt, and I will dignify this claim no further.” Responding to criticism about the weakening of the Pentagon’s civilian-harm-mitigation efforts, a spokesperson had previously said that “the Department remains committed to minimizing civilian harm caused by military operations and to meeting all relevant statutory requirements.” [ Read: Why is the Pentagon afraid of the press? ] Article V Massie argues in this provision that Hegseth used the power of his office “in a manner that resulted in the extrajudicial killings of at least 243 persons aboard seagoing vessels alleged to be smuggling narcotics.” The military’s strikes on small boats off the coast of Latin America began in September 2025. The most recent strike, late last month, killed five people. The Trump administration has claimed that the strikes targeted boats transporting drugs for cartels. But officials have not presented evidence to substantiate that. Transporting drugs is not a capital offense under U.S. law. Hegseth “chilled independent legal review” in the Defense Department, Massie alleges, and relied on a “purported legal basis for the use of military force.” That refers to a memo from the Justice Department’s Office of Legal Counsel that reportedly recasts cartel associates as legitimate targets in an “armed conflict.” (The memo has not been made public.) Many legal experts, including former military lawyers, have described the boat-strike campaign as a clear violation of both U.S. and international law. Nor does it appear to have achieved its stated purpose of reducing the flow of drugs into the U.S.; some evidence suggests that the flow of cocaine has actually increased over the past year. Hegseth has defended the campaign as part of an effort to secure “our Homeland from the drugs that are killing our people.” And the White House had told us previously that the boat strikes reflect how “President Trump is using every tool at his disposal to save lives from the scourge of illicit narcotics.” Article VI Senator Mark Kelly of Arizona appeared in a video in November 2025 along with five other Democratic members of Congress who had served in national-security roles before taking office. They reminded members of the military and the intelligence community of their obligation to “refuse illegal orders.” Their message was posted on social media after the Trump administration had deployed troops in several U.S. cities and conducted more than 20 lethal strikes in the drug-boats campaign. Hegseth retaliated against Kelly with a formal letter of censure and directed the secretary of the Navy to review whether Kelly had engaged in “potentially unlawful” conduct. (Kelly served as a Navy pilot for more than two decades.) He has also threatened to reduce Kelly’s military-retirement rank and pay. The matter is being litigated in court. Massie accuses Hegseth of retaliation against a member of Congress for engaging in constitutionally protected speech and for exercising his responsibilities as a lawmaker. [ Read: ‘An example MUST BE SET’ ] Massie also argues that Hegseth ignored the separation of powers by placing the Department of Defense above the legislative and judicial branches. Hegseth, in turn, has accused Kelly of making “seditious” statements and said that he and the other lawmakers were “encouraging our warriors to ignore the orders of their Commanders,” which “sows doubt and confusion” and “only puts our warriors in danger.” Article VII Massie alleges that Hegseth overstepped his authority by using the Department of Defense to capture Maduro, the president of Venezuela, along with his wife, Cilia Flores. In the early hours of January 3, the U.S. military launched strikes across Venezuela and captured Maduro, transporting him to New York City, where he was indicted on multiple charges, including narcoterrorism. He awaits trial in a federal jail. Members of Congress, including senior lawmakers, learned about the seizure when the public did. The article claims that Hegseth violated his “constitutional duty to take care that the laws be faithfully executed,” because the U.S. had not declared war. The Trump administration has argued that no congressional notice was required because the strikes and the seizure of Maduro were a law-enforcement operation, not an act of war. (Trump also said that he kept members in the dark because “Congress has a tendency to leak.”) Massie argues that the real purpose of the operation was to control Venezuelan oil reserves and that it amounted to an act of war because it led to Venezuelan regime change and significant casualties. About 80 people, including civilians, were killed. Article VIII The final article accuses Hegseth of responsibility for civilian casualties and another unlawful war—in this case, in Yemen. By initiating and directing Operation Rough Rider—months of strikes against the Houthi rebel group in the spring of 2025—Hegseth violated the War Powers Resolution, Massie claims. The strikes led to the deaths of an estimated 224 civilians and hundreds of Houthi fighters. Massie argues that the operation was illegal because the administration bypassed required congressional authorization. He has an unusual primary source to reference: the Signal group chat in which Hegseth and other top administration officials coordinated the strikes—while unwittingly sharing their plans with the editor in chief of this magazine, Jeffrey Goldberg. In the chat, Vice President Vance wrote that “there is a strong argument” for delaying the operation by a month, and Joe Kent, then the acting chief of staff to the director of national intelligence, said, “There is nothing time sensitive driving the time line.” Hegseth himself at one point chimed in, saying that “we can easily pause” the plans. The administration has defended that operation as furthering American “national security and foreign policy interests.” In a letter to House Speaker Johnson in late March 2025, Trump wrote that Houthi militants had “perpetrated piratical aggressions” and continued to “threaten and attack United States forces” in and around Yemen, as well as “commercial vessels in one of the most important shipping lanes in the world.” Nancy A. Youssef and Missy Ryan contributed to this story .

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : Marie Sarr décroche l’or en taekwondo et entre dans l’histoire
items.description: Le Sénégal tient une nouvelle championne olympique de la jeunesse. Marie Sarr a remporté la médaille d’or dans la catégorie des moins de 55 kg en taekwondo, après sa victoire face à la Tunisienne Yasmine Haouani (2-1), ce mardi, à l’arène CID du Complexe sportif Iba Mar Diop. Ce sacre constitue la cinquième médaille d’or de la délégation sénégalaise aux Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. Marie Sarr a fait vibrer le public sénégalais en s’adjugeant le titre au terme d’une finale disputée face à la Tunisienne Yasmine Haouani. Portée par le soutien du public, la jeune combattante a su faire la différence pour monter sur la plus haute marche du podium. Elle remporte ainsi une médaille d’or historique pour le taekwondo sénégalais. La représentante nationale avait déjà affiché ses ambitions lors des tours précédents. En quarts de finale, elle avait éliminé la Jordanienne Laean Alrawashdeh (2-1), avant de dominer largement l’Américaine Karlee Vogel en demi-finale (2-0). Un parcours maîtrisé qui a trouvé son aboutissement avec cette victoire en finale. À travers cette consécration, Marie Sarr ajoute une nouvelle ligne au palmarès du sport sénégalais et confirme le potentiel de la relève nationale en taekwondo. Cette médaille d’or vient également s’ajouter à celle de bronze remportée par sa compatriote Daïda Touré dans la catégorie des plus de 63 kg. Une double performance qui met le taekwondo sénégalais à l’honneur lors de ces JOJ organisés à domicile. Avec ce cinquième titre olympique de la jeunesse, le Sénégal poursuit sa progression au tableau des médailles et peut désormais regarder vers la suite de la compétition avec de nouvelles ambitions. C.T.N

items.title: Une rencontre de sensibilisation autour de la réhabilitation du parc Oti-Kéran
items.description: Kantè, 10 nov. (ATOP) –Une rencontre de sensibilisation sur la réhabilitation du parc Oti-Kéran s’est tenue le mardi 10 novembre à Naboulgou dans le canton de Pessidè, à environ 35 Km au nord de Kantè. Cette rencontre est une initiative de la direction régionale en charge des Ressources forestières de la Kara en collaboration avec les autorités préfectorales de l’Oti-Sud et de la Kéran. L’objectif est d’intensifier la sensibilisation auprès des acteurs sur les dispositions prises par les autorités gouvernementales relatives à la réhabilitation de l’aire protégée. Les acteurs concernés sont aussi appelés à réfléchir aux approches de solutions participatives pour une sauvegarde de ce patrimoine naturel. Les différents intervenants notamment le directeur régional en charge des ressources forestières de la Kara, Lcl Afoda Chamsoudine, les préfets Sambiani Fékimani de l’Oti-Sud et Douti N’Sarma Mabiba de la Kéran ont réaffirmé l’engagement du gouvernement relatif au déguerpissement des éleveurs et agriculteurs de la réserve d’ici la fin de l’année. Suite à l’occupation illégale du parc, il s’agit pour les autorités gouvernementales de limiter les actions anthropiques sur ce patrimoine naturel en invitant les populations à adhérer à la politique gouvernementale dans la dynamique de l’aménagement du territoire, de la protection de l’environnement et de la restauration du couvert végétal. Malgré les efforts entrepris pour la conservation de sa biodiversité, le parc national Oti-Kéran a continué de subir de fortes pressions humaines. Ces principales actions anthropiques sont, entre autres, les pratiques agricoles, le surpâturage, le braconnage ainsi que l’exploitation du bois d’œuvre et du bois-énergie. L’utilisation non durable des ressources forestières, la carbonisation et les feux de végétation sont d’autres situations aggravantes. Les représentants des localités riveraines, notamment de Gando, Takpapiéni, N’Gambi, Sagbiébou et de Mogou du côté de l’Oti-Sud ainsi que de Naboulgou, Pessidè, Pangouda, Namouté et d’Ossacré du côté de la Kéran, ont également pris part à la rencontre. L’assistance a également été sensibilisée sur le phénomène de l’extrémisme violent, les valeurs du vivre-ensemble et de la cohésion sociale pour une paix et une sécurité durable. Créée à partir de la forêt classée de la Kéran, l’aire protégée Oti-Kéran, étendue de 1971 à 1976 à 163 640 hectares, est passée depuis 2016 à 69 000 ha. ATOP/PAP/MD

items.title: Jefferson Sackey declares intention for NPP Ablekuma Central primaries bid
items.description: Former Deputy Director of Communications at the Presidency, Jefferson Kwamina Sackey has declared his intention to contest the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) parliamentary primaries in Ablekuma Central, seeking a second nomination to lead the party’s bid to reclaim the seat in the 2028 general election. Mr Sackey brings experience in government communications, having worked on the Party’s presidential campaigns and serving as a Deputy Director of Communications for the NPP. He won the party’s Ablekuma Central parliamentary primary in 2023 and currently serves as a polling station chairman in Laterbiokorshie. In the 2024 parliamentary election, Sackey secured 32,735 votes, or 42.08 per cent of valid ballots. He drew 3,778 more votes than the NPP’s presidential candidate received in Ablekuma Central. The National Democratic Congress (NDC) incumbent, Abdul-Latif Dan, retained the seat with 45,066 votes. Closing the 12,331-vote gap in 2028 would require the party to retain that support and reach more voters across Ablekuma Central. His 2024 support provides a base for a renewed campaign.

items.title: Jospong Group showcases Ghanaian waste management solutions at COP31 in Türkiye
items.description: Ghanaian conglomerate Jospong Group of Companies is showcasing its waste management and recycling solutions at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, as it seeks to attract investment and expand its environmental services across Africa. The Group’s delegation, led by Executive Chairman Dr Joseph Siaw Agyepong, is engaging government representatives, investors and development partners on opportunities to develop integrated waste management infrastructure. The conference, which opened on November 9 and is scheduled to run until November 20, 2026, has brought together policymakers, climate experts, investors and private sector organisations to discuss climate action and sustainable development. Jospong says its participation is intended to highlight African-developed approaches to waste management and promote partnerships to address growing urban waste challenges. A major focus of the Group’s exhibition is its Integrated Recycling and Compost Plant (IRECOP), which is designed to process municipal solid waste through sorting, material recovery, recycling and compost production. The model seeks to recover useful materials from waste and reduce reliance on conventional landfill disposal. According to Jospong, the approach could also create employment, support agricultural production through compost supply and reduce greenhouse gas emissions associated with poorly managed waste. The Group is presenting the model to governments, municipal authorities, investors and development institutions as a potential option for cities seeking to improve sanitation and develop circular economy systems. The Group is also using the conference to pursue opportunities to expand its waste management operations and technical expertise beyond Ghana. Its stated expansion ambitions cover nearly 30 African countries, with interests and engagements in markets including Nigeria, Kenya, Angola, Liberia, Guinea, The Gambia and Togo. Jospong says it is seeking partnerships to develop integrated waste recovery facilities that can improve sanitation, create jobs and support investment in environmental services. Beyond showcasing its facilities, the Group says it wants to use COP31 to develop business relationships and secure partnerships that could support the expansion of its waste management operations. Its delegation includes representatives from Zoomlion Ghana Limited, IRECOP, Accra Compost and Recycling Plant (ACARP), Asian African Consortium and other businesses within its green transition portfolio. The Group is also building on earlier international climate engagements, including discussions at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 involving Switzerland’s Federal Office for the Environment and representatives of Jospong. Those engagements concerned a reported €20 million authorisation arrangement relating to internationally transferred mitigation outcomes (ITMOs) from the Group’s integrated recycling and composting facilities. From climate discussions to implementation Jospong says its participation at COP31 is aimed at positioning African technical expertise and private-sector investment as part of efforts to address environmental challenges. The Group is seeking to translate its engagements at the conference into partnerships and investment opportunities for waste management projects in Ghana and other African markets. The outcome of those discussions, including any agreements or investment commitments secured, will determine how far the conference advances the Group’s expansion plans.
